events.title: The Hotel Raid and the Agents' Arrival
events.summary: Four police officers breach Room 303 of the gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she raises her hands and submits. Outside, Agents Smith, Brown and Jones arrive and strip the operation from the Lieutenant, with Smith correcting the Lieutenant's belief that his men are bringing her down by telling him they are already dead. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches for the cuffs, Trinity moves inhumanly fast — palm, kick, snatch-twist-fire — and kills all four officers, ending as the sole survivor standing over the dead, physically unharmed and back in control. The two agents then split — Brown enters the hotel while Smith heads for the alley.
events.action: The raid's inversion — Trinity converts the cuff's first touch from the squad's finish into the trigger that kills all four officers, while the Agents seize the operation from the Lieutenant outside.

affects_outside.enables: The raid's failure and the Agents' takeover convert the story from containment to pursuit: Trinity is now a confirmed, uncatchable target the Agents must hunt, and the police are exposed as outmatched and expendable against her.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The police operation is spent — two units dead, the Lieutenant stripped of authority, the hotel room a crime scene the Agents now own.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Lieutenant's territorial pride is confirmed as a live, costly variable: Smith's belief that he could simply set the man aside is wrong, and the interference that already cost two units' lives will continue.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Four police officers breach Room 303 of the gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she submits. Outside, Agents Smith, Brown and Jones arrive and strip the operation from the Lieutenant, with Smith correcting the Lieutenant's belief that his men are winning by telling him they are already dead. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches for the cuffs Trinity moves: she kills all four officers and stands as the sole survivor. The two agents then split — Brown enters the hotel while Smith heads for the alley.

events.title: Trinity's Escape Across the Rooftops
events.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hardline is cut and redirects her to a phone at Wells and Lake, converting her from a cornered fighter into a runner with a worse, more distant exit. She runs the route — room to hall to fire escape to rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap and a 50-foot chasm — dives through a high window, and tumbles down a back stairwell crashing through glass and wood, arriving bleeding and broken but moving on the street at the Wells and Lake phone booth, then gone through the line. On the rooftops, a 40-foot leap that shatters the pursuing cops' physics is matched exactly by Agent Brown, who duplicates the impossible jump; the hotel police and rooftop cops are left stranded behind the gap. The Agents, left with only the wreckage of a smashed booth, learn the informant is real and that the crew's next target is Neo, so the hunt turns from Trinity to Neo.

state_triples.reading: Trinity believes Morpheus has the whole situation mapped and that his instructions are her only chance — but the event shows she is being driven into a desperate improvisation (a rooftop chase and a 50-foot jump) that no one has fully controlled. She also believes the Agents are a human-scale escalation she can outrun, betting her escape on the Matrix's physical limits holding against them — a bet Agent Brown shatters by duplicating her impossible leap, though she does not yet know Agents are programs who can rewrite those rules. Her escape reads to her as a clean win, when it is actually the seed of the net tightening around Neo, something she cannot see.

state_triples.reading: The rooftop cops believe Trinity is cornered — a woman who has run out of roof and will be caught or die at the edge — and that Agent Brown is simply the officer leading them, one of their own on their side of the human/physical line. Both beliefs are exactly backwards: the edge is her launch point, and Brown belongs to a category they cannot comprehend, as alien to them as the woman they're chasing. Their misjudgment of the jump is actually correct about everyone except Trinity and Brown — the gap that would kill them is trivial for those two — so their contempt is aimed at the only people in the chase who genuinely cannot follow.

affects_outside.enables: Trinity's escape preserves the one thread that lets the crew reach Neo first: she is the one who will shepherd Neo out (ev-005), so the 'small' win of her survival is the seed of the crew staying ahead of the machine's search. The event also establishes Morpheus as the guiding authority whose voice will later shepherd Neo the same way, and it confirms to the audience — through the impossible leap — that the Matrix's rules are breakable and that the Agents break them too.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The escape spends the crew's remaining margin: Trinity arrives bleeding and broken, the hardline network is compromised (the Wells/Lake phone is the last reachable exit), and the Agents now have the crew's next target. It costs the Agents nothing physical but converts their failure into a lead.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The machine's search apparatus turns its gaze from Trinity to Neo — the final image of the camera falling through the phone into a running 'search' and emerging onto a computer screen where a search engine runs is the surveillance state locking onto Neo, who becomes the axis of everything that follows. Cypher, the unseen informant, has traded his crew for his own return to the Matrix — a betrayal the Agents now act on but do not yet understand as a private deal.

She fights through the hotel — evading Agent Brown in the hall, forced upward on the fire escape by Agent Smith — and out onto the rooftops, where a 40-foot leap that shatters the pursuing cops' physics is matched exactly by Agent Brown. She clears a final 50-foot chasm, dives through a high window, and crashes down a stairwell, arriving on the street just in time to answer a ringing phone a heartbeat before a garbage truck obliterates the booth. She escapes. The Agents, left with only wreckage, learn the informant is real and that the crew's next target is Neo, so the machine's search turns from Trinity to Neo.

events.title: Neo Is Summoned and Meets Trinity
events.summary: An external party hijacks Neo's computer and summons him by name, then a planted symbol converts a routine black-market transaction into an abduction-by-invitation that draws him out of his apartment; at a crowded gathering, Trinity confirms she was on his machine, warns him he is watched and in danger, and converts his private obsession into a named quest — the question voiced and the promise that the answer will find him — before vanishing into the crowd. The event moves Neo from asleep-and-ordinary isolation into active, recruited motion toward a hidden resistance while the pursuit gains a target it has named.
events.action: Neo is contacted through his own machine, follows the planted signal out into the night, and is met by Trinity, who names his search and sets the hook without giving him the answer.

He reads the white rabbit pin as a coincidence precisely because he does not yet know he is being guided, and he treats his 'feeling of unrealness' as something he can joke away rather than the first edge of the truth he will spend the film confronting.

state_triples.reading: Trinity believes she is approaching a genuine seeker — someone the question has already brought this far, 'looking for him' — and treats her closeness and riddles as a calibrated recruitment technique. What she cannot yet know, and what the scene withholds from her, is that Neo is 'The One,' so she reads him as a promising recruit rather than the person the whole operation is built around; her confidence that she has time to finish the pitch is itself a gamble on seconds she may not have.

affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents, who already have 'The name is Neo' (sc-011) — this event advances the pursuit by moving its target out of passive isolation into visible motion, making him easier to track.

events.title: Neo's Capture at the Office
events.summary: Neo is woken by an alarm, reprimanded by his manager Rhineheart, and cryptically contacted by Morpheus, who warns him that 'they' are coming. A Federal Express Guy delivers a phone; a female employee points out Neo's cubicle; the Agents and cops raid the floor. Guided turn by turn by Morpheus's voice, Neo flees — hiding, freezing behind a cop, and climbing out onto the window ledge — but his nerve breaks and he retreats inside, the phone having fallen. He is left trapped in the office with a cop opening the door, aware he is hunted but unable to name who 'they' are.
events.action: The ordinary world reasserts control (Rhineheart's ultimatum), then a hidden war breaks in (the coordinated raid by the Agents and cops), and Neo is converted from a passive, cryptically-contacted employee into an active fugitive obeying commands under lethal pressure. His escape under Morpheus's remote guidance collapses at the one physical test it requires — the crossing to the ledge — and he is driven back into the corner, now exposed, his lifeline gone and Morpheus disconnected.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's failed escape delivers him into the Agents' custody, setting up the interrogation and physical-modification sequence that follows. It also proves that remote guidance and fear-driven compliance are insufficient — Morpheus will have to close the gap differently (the 'ready to see what I want to show you' education). The reprimand establishes the ordinary world's authority as petty and ultimately irrelevant to who Neo is, sharpening the irony that Rhineheart's accusation of 'specialness' is about to become true in a sense he cannot imagine.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's only escape route (the scaffold/ledge crossing) is lost when he drops the phone and retreats — the one exit Morpheus could vouch for is now closed, forcing him into enemy hands. Morpheus's belief that fear alone will make Neo compliant is partially disproven. Neo's trust in his own sense of insignificance is being violently dismantled, but he has not yet accepted that he is the someone they are looking for.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents now have Neo cornered on the office floor with no exit — their next move (the capture and interrogation) is set in motion entirely by this event's failure.

Whether RHINEHEART intends to fire NEO immediately if he is late again, or merely to warn him.
Whether the female employee who points out Neo's cubicle acts knowingly or incidentally.
What the Agents specifically intend to do to Neo, since Morpheus says 'I'm not sure what they're going to do.'
Whether Neo is actually in danger of dying from the height or whether this is an illusion within the Matrix.
Who 'they' are beyond the Agents and cops seen in the neighbouring scene.

events.boundary_reason: The workday sequence—reprimand, chase, failed leap, and capture—ends when Neo is taken into custody; the following scene is his interrogation, a distinct confrontation.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Neo is pulled from sleep into his ordinary workday, subjected to his manager's authority, then hunted by the Agents and guided into an escape by Morpheus that fails when he cannot trust himself to cross to the roof — leaving him cornered and delivered into enemy hands.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The ordinary world reasserts control over Neo (a reprimand), then a hidden war breaks into it (the Agents' raid), and Neo's attempt to flee under remote guidance collapses at the one physical test it requires. The event turns Neo from a passive, cryptically-contacted employee into a cornered fugitive who has failed his only way out.

events.title: The Interrogation
events.summary: The Agents seize Neo outside the skyscraper, force him into a sedan, and carry him into a white interrogation room, where Agent Smith offers him a bargain — betray Morpheus and his crimes are erased. When Neo refuses and asserts his rights, Smith drops the pretense of negotiation and, with the standing Agents pinning him down, physically violates him: sealing his mouth shut until it is gone and burrowing a fiber-optic wire-tap creature into his navel to force his cooperation. Watching from her motorcycle, Trinity sees the capture in her rearview mirror and reacts with a single dismayed curse.

state_triples.reading: The standing Agents believe Neo is a trivial, laughable target — the same man Morpheus has been hunting as 'The One' — so their derisive satisfaction is a misreading of exactly how significant the prisoner they are mocking actually is.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's capture and the implanted bug give the Agents a means to track him — and through him, potentially Morpheus and the resistance — so the violation becomes the physical debt the story must later repay.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's freedom and bodily autonomy are spent; his refusal to betray Morpheus has cost him his intact body and left him in the Agents' control.

events.title: Neo Chooses to Meet Morpheus
events.summary: A tapped phone call converts Neo's private terror into a fated commitment: an unseen voice names him 'the One,' tells him the danger is himself, reminds him of a 'road' he already knows, and extracts a single 'Yes' to a meeting at the Adams Street bridge before the line is cut. Trinity's car collects him from the street; the crew holds him at gunpoint and orders him to strip for a bug-extraction, and when Switch's ultimatum fails, Trinity's appeal to the 'road' Neo already knows persuades him to close the door and stay. The car then carries him through the wet underworld, leaving the ordinary world behind.
events.action: Morpheus phones Neo, names him 'the One,' reframes the danger as Neo himself, and extracts his consent to a meeting before the tapped line is cut; Trinity's car collects Neo from the bridge; the crew restrains him at gunpoint and orders him to strip for an extraction; Switch's ultimatum fails, and Trinity's appeal persuades Neo to close the door and stay rather than flee; the car drives off into the night.

registers.entry: Woken screaming from a nightmare, briefly reassured his body is intact at home.
registers.change: Jolted by the ringing phone into dread and compulsion, pulled out of bed; later held at gunpoint and ordered to strip.
registers.exit: Dressed and in a moving car, having submitted to restraint and a pending extraction.

registers.entry: Confused about what is happening to him, asking 'What the hell is happening to me?'
registers.change: Told he is 'the One' and that Morpheus has spent his life searching for him; then told the danger is himself and reminded of a 'road' he already knows.
registers.exit: Reframes his resistance as self-destructive but still ignorant of what 'meeting' entails or what awaits at the bridge.

registers.entry: A hunted man alone, treating Morpheus as the authority who can explain his life.
registers.change: Commits to Morpheus with '... Yes'; then becomes a captive of Trinity's crew, held at gunpoint, before choosing to stay with them.
registers.exit: A compliant, if confused, follower of the crew — Trinity established as his guide, Switch as his antagonist.

registers.entry: Raw and destabilized — terror, then brief relief, then dread.
registers.change: Sickened by being named 'the One'; cornered and humiliated under armed guard; then persuaded by Trinity's appeal.
registers.exit: Resigned and committed — closing the door as a surrender he frames to himself as a choice.

registers.entry: Alone and exposed on the rain-soaked street, feeling watched.
registers.change: A car slides to a stop beside him and its back door opens, offering escape or capture; then held at gunpoint inside.
registers.exit: In the moving car, committed to whatever lies ahead — no longer exposed on the street but no longer free.

registers.entry: A 'nobody' (his own self-concept from the ledge).
registers.change: Declared 'the One' by Morpheus — important enough that the Agents would have killed him — then treated as a dangerous liability by Switch and a prophesied asset by Trinity.
registers.exit: Held between two readings of his importance: Switch's contempt and Trinity's faith — neither yet resolved for Neo himself.

registers.entry: In bed at home.
registers.change: Answering the phone, then directed to the Adams Street bridge; collected by Trinity's car; held inside it.
registers.exit: Being driven through the wet underworld, having left the ordinary world behind.

state_triples.reading: Neo believes he is making a choice — answering 'Yes,' then closing the car door — but each 'choice' is engineered: Morpheus forces a yes/no under a closing window, and Trinity makes staying feel marginally less like falling than bolting into the rain. He reframes capitulation as agency to preserve a shred of dignity, unaware he is consenting to have his entire known life dismantled.

registers.entry: Unseen, on the tapped phone line.
registers.change: None — he remains off-screen, communicating only by voice.
registers.exit: Unseen, on the tapped phone line.
registers.unchanged_because: The scene keeps him entirely as a voice (V.O.); he never appears or moves in space.

registers.entry: A distant hunter who has spent his life searching for Neo.
registers.change: Declares Neo 'the One,' reframes the Agents' visit as their mistake, and extracts Neo's consent to meet.
registers.exit: Established as the authority whose faith project now has a committed subject — Neo has said 'Yes.'

registers.entry: Working against a closing window — the line is tapped and could be traced.
registers.change: Delivers his message and hangs up the instant he gets 'Yes,' before the line can be traced.

registers.entry: Knows Neo is 'the One' and that the Agents underestimated him.

registers.entry: Controlled urgency layered over conviction.
registers.change: None — his composure holds throughout the call.
registers.exit: Controlled urgency layered over conviction.

registers.entry: The prophet/authority who has been searching.

registers.exit: The prophet/authority who has been searching.
registers.unchanged_because: His declaration of Neo's identity confirms his own role rather than changing it.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus believes Neo will say yes when offered the meeting, and he is right in outcome — but he is reading Neo through prophecy, not through the frightened, sick person on the line. His confidence is correct but blind to how little Neo understands or wants any of it; Neo agrees from vertigo, not conviction.

registers.entry: Absent, only watching Neo's capture from afar.
registers.change: Drives up in the car on the bridge and opens the back door to collect him; later sits with him inside the car.
registers.exit: Present in the moving car with Neo and the crew, directly intervening.

registers.entry: A distant watcher of Neo.
registers.change: Becomes his direct intervener and, when Switch's force fails, his persuader — arguing against brute force and appealing to his self-knowledge.
registers.exit: Established as Neo's guide and protector — the one who argues he is worth gentle coercion because he is 'the One.'

registers.entry: An observer with no direct authority over Neo yet.
registers.change: Takes command of the persuasion — overriding Switch's ultimatum with the appeal that actually works.
registers.exit: The effective authority in the car — her method, not Switch's, delivers compliance.

registers.entry: Calm, controlled urgency — part duty, part investment in Neo as 'the One.'

registers.exit: Calm, controlled urgency — part duty, part investment in Neo as 'the One.'

But she is acting on faith Morpheus placed in her, blind to whether Neo is truly 'the One' — the entire arc the story is setting up.

registers.entry: An armed guard enforcing the group's will on a defiant Neo.

registers.exit: His ultimatum has failed — Neo resists his brute force, and Trinity's softer method takes over.

registers.entry: Reads Neo as a dangerous, ignorant 'coppertop' — a liability to be broken.

registers.exit: Reads Neo as a dangerous, ignorant 'coppertop' — a liability to be broken.
registers.unchanged_because: The scene shows no shift in Switch's reading of Neo; his method is pure coercion throughout.

registers.entry: Impatience sharpened into contempt.

registers.exit: Impatience sharpened into contempt.
registers.unchanged_because: No shift in Switch's affect is recorded; he remains the aggressor in contrast to Trinity.

His contempt blinds him to why the others treat this captive with such care.

affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents, who lost their quarry: Neo has slipped from their grasp into Morpheus's crew, so the pursuit now has a target it has lost.

events.turns_on: The ringing phone — a tapped line that forces Morpheus to be brief and to extract a single 'Yes' under a closing window, converting Neo's shapeless terror into a fated commitment; and the car door, which Neo opens to flee and then closes to stay — the physical pivot on which his capitulation turns into a choice.

events.title: The Red Pill
events.summary: In a moving car, Trinity and Switch extract a tracking bug from Neo's body by suction and electrocution, then drive him to the Hotel Lafayette, where Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong unease as proof of an enslaving illusion and offers him a choice of pills; Neo swallows the red pill, and the crew uses it as a trace program that disrupts his signal and lets them locate his real body, but as the mirror-liquid invades him his vitals fail and he goes into cardiac arrest, blacking out while the operation races to complete the lock.
events.action: extraction → transit → recruitment → trace/unplugging begins. The abstract chase is converted into physical fact (the bug), then into an irreversible self-chosen commitment (the red pill as a trace program), then into a bodily crisis as the trace program locates Neo's real body and the mirror-liquid invasion drives him into cardiac arrest.

registers.entry: Intact but carrying an internal tracking bug beneath his skin (carried from the chase).
registers.change: The bug is extracted by suction and electrocution; later his real body is subjected to the trace program as the mirror-liquid invades him and his vitals fail.
registers.exit: Relieved of the external tracker but in cardiac arrest as the mirror gel crawls over him and his body arches in agony before blacking out.

registers.entry: Ignorant of what is being done to him and why, asking 'What is this thing?'.
registers.change: Learns he is bugged and sees the bug is real; then learns the Matrix is an illusory prison for the mind and that his lifelong unease pointed to it; then learns the pill is a trace program that disrupts his signal.
registers.exit: Knows he is targeted and that 'something is wrong with the world' has a name and a mechanism, but cannot reconcile the dissolving reality he is being pulled through.

registers.entry: A fugitive in the crew's custody, moving through the night.
registers.change: Delivered from the car to the Hotel Lafayette, seated before Morpheus, then wired into a chair in the equipment room.
registers.exit: Located and hardwired into the crew's system, his real-world position pinned for extraction.

registers.entry: Under the crew's control but being painfully violated by the extraction.
registers.change: Passes from monitored procedure into medical crisis as the trace program triggers fibrillation and cardiac arrest.
registers.exit: In life-threatening arrest, the operation racing to complete the lock before he dies.

registers.entry: Distrustful of Trinity, having been held at gunpoint by the crew (carried from the standoff).
registers.change: Bonded to the crew through the shared, painful secret of the bug; vouched for by Trinity before Morpheus; accepted by Morpheus as a recruit.
registers.exit: A committed recruit under the crew's protection and authority, though Cypher still regards him as a routine mark.

registers.entry: A legendary hacker / fugitive 'coppertop' liability.
registers.change: Reframed by Morpheus from fan meeting his idol into a self-chosen recruit who has crossed an irreversible threshold.
registers.exit: A committed candidate being unplugged — no longer a legend but a body on the table whose potential the crew is now betting on.

registers.entry: Terrified, violated, bewildered during the extraction.
registers.change: Moves through awe at the bug's reality, acute anxiety before Morpheus, overwhelmed exposure during the choice, and vertiginous terror as his senses dissolve.
registers.exit: Panic and bodily revolt ('Uh-oh', 'It's cold') overtaken entirely by the agony of arrest.

state_triples.reading: Neo believes he is being offered a genuine, free choice ('nothing more than the truth') when in fact he is being steered through an engineered, irreversible recruitment whose true cost — the loss of his body and any return — has been withheld from him.

registers.entry: Neo's captor-hander, having held him at gunpoint and then extracted him (carried from the standoff and the car).
registers.change: Escalates to electrocuting Neo to save him; vouches for him before Morpheus; then becomes his monitor as his body fails.
registers.exit: The crew member fighting to keep Neo alive through a procedure that is turning lethal, her personal investment ahead of any proof he is 'the One'.

registers.entry: Driving/operating in the car with Switch.
registers.change: Transits Neo to the Hotel Lafayette, delivers him to Morpheus, then works the monitors in the equipment room.
registers.exit: At her station reading Neo's failing vitals while the crew completes the lock.

registers.entry: The field operative who disobeyed to bring Neo in (carried from the standoff).
registers.change: Completes her half of the handoff and returns to her technical role monitoring his body.
registers.exit: Back in her crew function as medical monitor, her judgment of Neo now staked before Morpheus.

registers.entry: Focused urgency, overriding Neo's pain during the extraction.
registers.change: Shifts from calm directive control to tightening alarm as his vitals collapse.
registers.exit: Trained exterior over mounting alarm, reporting his failing body in clinical terms without comforting him.

registers.entry: Knows the Matrix is an illusion and the crew's mission to free minds (carried from the chase).
registers.change: No new knowledge gained or lost in this event.
registers.exit: Knows the Matrix is an illusion and the crew's mission to free minds (carried from the chase).
registers.unchanged_because: The event turns on Neo's discovery, not Trinity's; she already holds this knowledge and nothing challenges or extends it here.

registers.entry: Secure inside the moving car and the crew's operation (carried from the escape).
registers.change: No threat lands on Trinity herself in this event.
registers.exit: Secure inside the moving car and the crew's operation (carried from the escape).
registers.unchanged_because: The danger in this event falls entirely on Neo's body; Trinity's own safety is not tested or altered.
registers.exit_asserted: Secure inside the crew's operation.

registers.entry: Capable and uninjured, running the extraction (carried from the chase).
registers.change: No physical change to Trinity is recorded.
registers.exit: Capable and uninjured, running the extraction (carried from the chase).
registers.unchanged_because: Nothing in the scenes records a physical change to Trinity.
registers.exit_asserted: Capable and uninjured, running the monitors.

state_triples.reading: Trinity believes Neo is worth vouching for and may be 'the one' — a wager she is staking rather than something the event confirms, and one that runs ahead of any proof.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's real-world body is now located and being unplugged, which sets up his awakening in the pod (the next event) and the crew's flight once the Agents trace him.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The irreversible commitment is made — there is no return to Neo's old life; and the trace program that locates him also risks exposing the crew's position.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Cypher's dismissiveness toward Neo as 'just another Dorothy' is seeded here as the fault line for his later betrayal.

events.turns_on: the red pill (and its twin, the blue pill)

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo survives the cardiac arrest or what exactly lies in the darkness he is swallowed into.
Whether the mirror's liquefaction is a physical event in the room or a manifestation inside Neo's perception of the Matrix.
What 'Tank' and 'the signal' concretely are beyond Morpheus's call for them.
Whether 'He' in Trinity's advice ('He knows more than you can possibly imagine') refers to the Oracle or someone else.

events.boundary_reason: Arrival at the Hotel Lafayette reframes the question to 'will Neo commit to the truth?' — the meeting with Morpheus, the choice of pills, and the trace program that pulls him out of the Matrix answer that together. The unit closes when he blacks out, severed from the Matrix.

events.title: Born Into the Real World
events.summary: Neo ruptures the shroud of his pod in the machine power plant; a machine disconnects him—spinning open the cable lock, disengaging the coaxial, sliding the needle and cerebrum-chip free, and snapping the hoses—then sucks him out, whether to free or harvest him unclear. He is flushed through the waste pipe and grease traps into the sewer main, snatched by a cable into a flying machine, and hauled aboard a hovercraft, where he is raised to face Morpheus, who names him and welcomes him into the real world, before Neo passes out.
events.action: A body trapped and submerged in a magenta amnion fights blindly against the gelatin, unable to breathe, then ruptures the elastic shroud and tears himself free, emerging bald, naked, slick with gelatin, dizzy and nauseous but able to suck for air. A machine drops in, seizes and paralyzes him, spins open the cable lock, disengages the coaxial from the base of his skull, slides the needle and cerebrum-chip free with blood and spinal fluid, snaps the hoses, and opens the back of the unit so the vacuum sucks him out. He falls and slides through the waste pipe and grease traps, is carried to the sewer main, is snatched by a metallic cable into a flying machine, is lowered by a harness onto the hovercraft floor, and is raised to face Morpheus, who smiles, welcomes him, and names him and the real world; Neo then passes out.
locations: POWER PLANT - CLOSE ON MAN'S BODY

registers.exit: Disconnected from the capsule and no longer physically plugged in, but his fate — freed or harvested — remains undetermined.

registers.entry: Suspended inside the pod in the power plant.

events.title: Waking in the Real World
events.summary: Neo is recovered from the sewer and wakes aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, where his atrophied body is rebuilt with acupuncture-like needles and grafted hardware, then reoriented across roughly two centuries as Morpheus identifies him as the one the search sought. The event moves Neo from unconscious recovery through physical reconstruction to the threshold of being shown reality, and it fixes Morpheus's governing method: he will show rather than explain, deferring the larger truth as something to be demonstrated. Trinity's doubt that the search may have failed is overruled by Morpheus's certainty but left unanswered; Dozer treats Neo as a patient under repair, not someone to be briefed.
events.action: Neo is recovered, physically rebuilt with grafted hardware, reoriented across two centuries, and led by Morpheus toward a demonstration of reality that replaces explanation.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Neo surfaces from the rescue into consciousness aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, where Morpheus confirms the search succeeded and begins rebuilding Neo's atrophied body, then reorients him across two centuries and leads him toward a demonstration of reality that will replace explanation. The event moves Neo from unconscious recovery through physical reconstruction to the threshold of ontological revelation, and it fixes Morpheus's governing method: he will show rather than tell.

events.title: The Desert of the Real
events.summary: Morpheus guides Neo into an ecto-skeleton chair on the main deck and feeds a coaxial line into the jack at the back of his neck; with a loud click Neo is jacked in and taken into the Construct, where Morpheus lays out the full revelation — the Matrix as a neural-interactive simulation overlaying a scorched real world in which humans are grown in fields and farmed as a power source, crystallized in the image of a fetus plucked from its stalk by a harvesting machine. Neo resists and demands to be let out, but the revelation cannot be stopped; on his return to the ship he thrashes, tears the cable from his neck, vomits, and blacks out. Trinity unlocks the cable and steadies him while Dozer holds him down, leaving Neo collapsed and unconscious on the deck — having crossed from one who was told the truth to one who physically rejected it and must now survive it.

events.boundary_reason: The question shifts to 'what is the Matrix, really?' — the crew intro, jacking in, Morpheus's history of the Construct, the fetus fields, and the power plant, culminating in Neo's rejection and physical collapse back on the deck. This is one sustained revelation that ends when his body rejects the truth.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Morpheus jacks Neo into the ship's systems and, inside the Construct, delivers the full revelation of what the Matrix is and what the real world has become — a neural-interactive simulation overlaying a scorched wasteland where humanity is farmed as a power source. Neo resists, demands to be let out, and his mind's refusal manifests physically on the ship: he thrashes, rips at the cable, vomits, and blacks out, crossing the irreversible threshold from being told the truth to having survived it.
prose_before_reconcile.action: guided revelation -> physical rejection of the truth -> collapse
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: the revelation of the truth about the Matrix

events.title: The Prophecy and the Operator
events.summary: In the dark of Neo's room, Morpheus reframes Neo's traumatic, involuntary rescue as destiny: he apologizes for breaking the rule against freeing older minds, recounts the myth of the One — a man born inside the Matrix who could remake it, who freed the first of them and taught them the truth, and whom the Oracle prophesied would return to destroy the Matrix and end the war — and reveals that he believes 'the search is over,' i.e. that Neo himself is this One, before leaving him to rest for his training. After a beat of the hovercraft's lights flickering on, Tank enters, introduces himself as Neo's operator, and by revealing that he is 'born free' (a genuine child of Zion, without jacks) and describing Zion as the last human city, gives Neo his first solid facts about the real world and its people, then urges that training begin with 'we got a lot to do, so let's get to it.'
events.action: Morpheus converts Neo's rescue into a prophecy and names Neo its object, repositioning himself from captor-debtor into guide and true believer; Tank then converts the abstract prophecy into a human, relational world — establishing kinship through shared 'born free' humanity and his role as operator — and moves Neo toward training.

registers.entry: A newly freed man who knows only that he has been pulled out of one reality and cannot return to it, unsure what he has been drawn into.
registers.change: Learns the origin myth of the One — a man born inside the Matrix who could remake it, who freed the first of them and taught them the truth, and whom the Oracle prophesied would return to destroy the Matrix and end the war — and that Morpheus believes 'the search is over,' i.e. that Neo himself is this One. Then learns from Tank that the newcomer is his operator, that some humans are 'born free' without jacks, and that Zion is 'the last human city,' the only place humans have left.
registers.exit: Knows the prophecy of the One and that he is being positioned as its fulfillment, and holds his first concrete facts about the real world — its operator role, Zion, and humans born free of the Matrix — yet still does not understand the larger structure (the war, Zion's place in it).

registers.entry: Regards Morpheus as a captor-custodian who has done something irreversible and dangerous to him.
registers.change: Morpheus reframes himself from captor to debtor-and-guide (apology plus a lifelong purpose), and Neo offers no argument against the prophecy, accepting the reframe passively. Then Tank, a stranger, establishes kinship through a handshake and shared 'born free' humanity, and Neo performs the cooperative-recruit ritual, letting himself be led.
registers.exit: Relates to Morpheus as the guide of a destiny rather than merely the author of a trauma, and has begun to extend trust to Tank as a warm, trustworthy human face — trust grounded only in friendliness, not yet tested.

registers.entry: Raw, emptied, and half-dissolved by what he was shown and by the physical rejection of it; grieving a lost world and bracing against the fact that there is no return.
registers.change: No new emotional resolution is reached; the prophecy and the new facts land on a man still in shock, and neither scene moves him out of it.
registers.exit: Raw, emptied, and half-dissolved by what he was shown and by the physical rejection of it; grieving a lost world and bracing against the fact that there is no return.
registers.unchanged_because: The event gives Neo meaning (destiny) and new facts, but no scene shows him settling emotionally; his near-silence and short, stunned questions show the same destabilized state he entered in.

registers.entry: A victim of an experiment — the object of an irreversible, rule-breaking procedure.
registers.change: Morpheus repositions him as the object of a prophecy ('the search is over'), and Tank repositions him as a recruit with a role ('your operator') and a destination, closing with 'let's get to it' to convert wonder into momentum toward training.
registers.exit: Positioned as the prophesied One and as a recruit about to begin training, with an operator assigned to handle his connection.

registers.entry: Physically contained aboard the hovercraft after the pod-extraction, but existentially unsafe — his entire model of reality has dissolved and every answer opens a larger unknown.
registers.change: Tank's warmth and the handshake offer the appearance of a safe guide, but nothing in the scenes confirms that Neo's world has become safe; the unknowns (war, Zion, the prophecy) only widen.
registers.exit: Physically contained aboard the hovercraft after the pod-extraction, but existentially unsafe — his entire model of reality has dissolved and every answer opens a larger unknown.
registers.unchanged_because: Friendliness is offered as reassurance, but no scene establishes that Neo is actually safer or that the threats he faces have receded; his trust in Tank is an extrapolation from warmth, not a change in his actual condition.
registers.exit_asserted: Physically contained aboard the hovercraft, but existentially unsafe — his entire model of reality has dissolved and every answer opens a larger unknown.

registers.entry: An unremarkable, newly extracted mind — the latest rule-breaking rescue.
registers.change: Morpheus elevates him, by belief, from 'another freed prisoner' to the fulfillment of a lifelong quest — the One whose coming was prophesied.
registers.exit: Invested, on the strength of Morpheus's faith, with the status of the prophesied One — a status not yet earned or verified, but now actively conferred.

state_triples.reading: Neo accepts the prophecy passively rather than embracing it — his 'I can't go back, can I?' is a question of loss, not ambition, and his 'For what?' is receptivity, not consent. He is letting himself be positioned as the One without yet agreeing to be it; he believes he is being offered a purpose that explains his rescue, but has not grasped that he is being made the instrument of someone else's faith.

registers.entry: An apologetic rule-breaker who has endangered Neo and owes him an explanation.

registers.exit: Established as Neo's guide and the standard-bearer of the prophecy — the man who will make his belief that 'the search is over' true through the training to come.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus is steadying himself as much as Neo. The apology is half-confession, and the myth is the ground he stands on when the ethics of his choice get shaky; he needs Neo to accept the rescue as destiny so that his own gamble is vindicated. His certainty about 'the search is over' is faith placed ahead of evidence, and he will spend the coming events trying to make it true.

state_triples.reading: Tank believes friendliness and a shared handshake will warm Neo into readiness, underestimating how shattered Neo still is; he frames the prophecy as 'an exciting time,' unaware that for Neo it is a death sentence of responsibility layered on top of a world he has just lost.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's training (the Dojo, skills downloads, the rooftop jump) — the event installs the operator (Tank), the destination (Zion), the role (the One), and the mentor's conviction that makes the training meaningful rather than merely coercive.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Any possibility of Neo returning to his old life is now closed off as a hope; Morpheus has staked his authority and faith on Neo being the One, so the coming tests will either vindicate or expose that belief.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: None recorded — no character outside this event is shown reacting to it.

events.turns_on: the prophecy of the One and Morpheus's belief that 'the search is over'

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo is actually the One.
Who, if anyone, is present in the hovercraft during the lights-flickering beat (sc-046).
Whether the fluorescent lights coming on is manual or automatic.
Whether the lights mark morning or merely the end of a rest period.

events.boundary_reason: After the collapse, the story pivots to a new question — 'What is Neo's purpose here?' Morpheus reframes the rescue as the fulfillment of the One prophecy and promises training (sc-045), then Tank arrives to introduce himself, Zion, and the 'born free' concept before urging they begin (sc-047). This is the calm setup between the revelation and the actual training.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: In the dark of Neo's room, Morpheus reframes Neo's traumatic, involuntary rescue as destiny: he apologizes for breaking the rule against freeing older minds, recounts the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy that he will return to destroy the Matrix and end the war, and reveals that he believes 'the search is over' — that Neo is the One — before leaving him to rest for his training. After a beat of the hovercraft's lights flickering on, Tank enters, introduces himself as Neo's operator, and by revealing that he is 'born free' (a genuine child of Zion, without jacks) and describing Zion as the last human city, gives Neo his first solid facts about the real world and its people, then urges that training begin.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Morpheus converts Neo's rescue into a prophecy and names Neo its object; Tank then converts the abstract prophecy into a human, relational world and moves Neo toward training.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: the prophecy of the One and Morpheus's belief that 'the search is over'

events.title: Kung Fu and the First Sparring Lesson
events.summary: Tank loads Neo's combat skills out of the prescribed order, treating the download as a game, and Neo — euphoric from possessing jujitsu and kung fu — believes he has arrived at real skill. Morpheus meets his declaration with a flat 'Show me' and, in the sparring program, dismantles him: every furious attack is blocked, his body is beaten down until he spits blood, and he is forced to concede Morpheus is too fast. Under rage Neo lands one clean blow that knocks Morpheus's glasses off. Morpheus, unharmed and pleased, reframes himself as a guide who can only show Neo the door — the journey is Neo's to make — and orders Tank to load the jump program.
events.action: out-of-order download -> declaration -> sparring and defeat -> breakthrough blow -> handoff -> advance to jump program

registers.entry: Has combat skills (jujitsu, kung fu, etc.) downloaded into him but believes possessing the program equals being able to use it.
registers.change: Learns through repeated defeat that the download gives moves but not mastery, and that the simulation's rules are computer rules that 'can be bent' and some 'can be broken' — a truth he only half-accepts.
registers.exit: Knows intellectually that the rules are mental and bendable, but has not yet embodied that understanding; still fighting largely as if physics are real constraints.

registers.entry: Intact, euphoric from the download ('looks like he just orgasmed').
registers.change: Overwhelmed and beaten down in the spar — falls to hands and knees, spits blood onto the white floor, takes stinging slaps and a blow to the head.
registers.exit: Bruised and bloodied but functional; the pain is real to him even though he is beginning to suspect it need not be.

registers.entry: A trainee who has just declared 'I know kung fu' and expects to be celebrated.
registers.change: Is dismantled by Morpheus, forced to admit 'You're too fast,' then, under rage, lands a single clean blow that knocks Morpheus's glasses off.
registers.exit: Has proven he can land a hit on Morpheus, but remains the dominated student; the burden of the journey has now been placed on him ('you're the one that has to step through').

registers.entry: Treats Morpheus as a teacher he can test himself against and expects shared excitement over his new skill.
registers.change: Meets Morpheus's flat 'Show me' and then a brutal, Socratic beating; still suspects Morpheus is 'doing something to him' and tries to name the maneuver.
registers.exit: Told by Morpheus that he is not acting on Neo but only 'freeing his mind' and showing the door; the relationship is reframed from manipulator/subject to guide/student, though Neo has not yet accepted the reframe.

registers.entry: Giddy empowerment and delight ('Holy shit! ... Hell yes!').
registers.change: Confidence collides with defeat — humiliation, frustration, fear, and rage as his borrowed skill is neutralized blow after blow.
registers.exit: Rage has cooled into wary defensiveness; he reaches for suspicion ('I know what you're trying to do') as the one thing he thinks he still controls.

registers.entry: The celebrated 'One' / promising blank slate in the eyes of the crew.
registers.change: Is reduced to a beaten, blood-spitting student whose every blow is blocked, watched by the whole crew as entertainment.
registers.exit: Has regained standing by landing the blow that earns Morpheus's genuine pleasure and moves the training forward, but is still the learner being directed.

registers.entry: Safe — the download is a painless, pleasurable event.
registers.change: Discovers that pain in the program is real to his mind/body — he bleeds and is overwhelmed — undermining his sense that this is a safe shortcut.
registers.exit: Only beginning to suspect the air (and thus the danger) 'isn't real'; his sense of safety is cracked but not yet rewritten.

state_triples.reading: Neo believes the instantaneous download means he has arrived at genuine skill — that 'knowing kung fu' is a completed fact — and that Morpheus will share his triumph. Both beliefs are wrong: he has information, not mastery, and Morpheus meets his declaration with a test, not a celebration. His arc here is the painful collapse of the equation between possessing knowledge and being able to perform it under pressure.

registers.entry: Observer arriving only to inquire about Neo's state ('How is he?').
registers.change: Moves from observer to instructor ('Show me'), then to sparring partner who dominates and teaches through the body, then back to director who orders the next stage.
registers.exit: Back in command of the session, having shifted from physical combat to directing Tank to load the jump program.

registers.entry: The skeptic-instructor whose belief in Neo as the One is still unconfirmed and who withholds celebration until ability is demonstrated.
registers.change: Subjects Neo's claim to a physical test, beats him into a reluctant half-understanding, then feels genuine pleasure and vindication when Neo lands the blow.
registers.exit: His faith is confirmed enough to smile and reframe himself as a guide who can 'only show you the door'; he places the responsibility for the journey on Neo while retaining authority over the training.

registers.entry: Serene and unhurried; his body shows a 'slow and steady rhythm' while Neo's is chaotic.
registers.change: Dominates the exchange with effortless blocking, then is struck on the side of the head by Neo, his glasses knocked off.
registers.exit: Physically unharmed but visibly marked by the hit (rubs his face); the blow confirms rather than threatens him.

registers.entry: The unquestioned authority whose superiority is demonstrated by effortless defense.
registers.change: Is momentarily struck — his glasses knocked off — a visible crack in his invulnerability witnessed by the crew.
registers.exit: Authority restored and even strengthened: he converts Neo's hit into proof his method works, smiling and directing the next stage without loss of command.

registers.entry: Already knows the rules of the simulation are mental and bendable; knows the gap between him and Neo; knows his teaching method.
registers.change: None — he teaches this truth rather than learning it.
registers.exit: Already knows the rules of the simulation are mental and bendable; knows the gap between him and Neo; knows his teaching method.
registers.unchanged_because: This event is Morpheus imparting knowledge, not acquiring it; his model of the simulation and of how to teach it is stable throughout.
registers.exit_asserted: Still knows the rules are bendable and that Neo has not yet grasped this; his understanding is unchanged.

registers.entry: Watchful, reverent anticipation; disciplined calm over a man who has wagered his purpose on Neo.
registers.change: Feels genuine pleasure and quiet vindication when Neo lands the blow.
registers.exit: Pleased but disciplined — he converts the pleasure immediately into the next instruction rather than lingering in it.

registers.entry: Never at risk — he holds Neo at arm's length deliberately and shows no strain.
registers.change: None — even the blow that knocks off his glasses does not threaten him.
registers.exit: Never at risk — he holds Neo at arm's length deliberately and shows no strain.
registers.unchanged_because: Morpheus is operating far above Neo throughout; the spar is instruction, not a real fight, and the single hit he takes is absorbed without consequence.
registers.exit_asserted: Still entirely safe and in control.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus believes Neo is, or is becoming, the One, and that 'freeing the mind' rather than forcing it is the right method — but he withholds verbal confirmation until ability is demonstrated ('Show me'). His calm certainty masks a wager: he is betting that physical overwhelm will force understanding faster than explanation could, and that Neo is ready to be pushed this hard. Neo's suspicion that Morpheus is 'doing something to him' is exactly the illusion Morpheus is trying to dissolve.

registers.entry: Obligated to load the operations programs in order; treats training as a game he gets to shape.
registers.change: Abandons the prescribed order for his own amusement, loading combat (jujitsu) first over Neo's weak protest.
registers.exit: Has set the training onto the combat track out of sequence, prioritizing spectacle over procedure.

registers.entry: Operator reporting status up the chain ('Ten hours straight. He's a machine.').
registers.change: Recedes as Morpheus and Neo take the foreground, then becomes the named recipient of Morpheus's order to load the next program.
registers.exit: Directed to 'load the jump program'; presumed to comply and move the training to its next stage.

registers.entry: Genuinely excited and curious — about the novelty of teaching and about what the 'One' can do; treats the download as a game.
registers.change: Feels pride and fascination watching Neo endure ('He's a machine'), then operator's satisfaction at a real breakthrough.
registers.exit: Alert and ready at the console, channeling that satisfaction into his function as he receives the order to load the jump program.

registers.entry: Safe at his operator station on the main deck, monitoring the simulation from outside it.
registers.change: None — he is an observer of the fight, not a participant in it.
registers.exit: Safe at his operator station on the main deck, monitoring the simulation from outside it.
registers.unchanged_because: Tank never enters the sparring program; he only watches the biometric readouts from the main deck.
registers.exit_asserted: Still safe at his station.

registers.entry: The crew's operator — the one who loads programs and reads the systems.
registers.change: None — he performs the same function throughout (loading, monitoring, executing orders).
registers.exit: The crew's operator — the one who loads programs and reads the systems.
registers.unchanged_because: His role is constant across the event; he is the consistent technical agent rather than someone whose standing shifts.
registers.exit_asserted: Still the operator, now directed to load the next program.

registers.entry: A booster who believes Neo is a promising blank slate — possibly the One — and treats his training as a fun reveal.
registers.change: Reads Neo's download-tolerance and endurance as evidence of destiny ('a machine'), running ahead of proof.
registers.exit: Still a believer, now with the crew's collective awe (gasps, Mouse's disbelief) backing his read; his belief matches Morpheus's wager but remains unconfirmed.

state_triples.reading: Tank believes Neo is a promising blank slate — possibly the One — and that the training will be a fun reveal of hidden capability. His lightness is partly a miscalibration of what's coming: he is treating this as a game and a spectacle, not yet knowing how much Neo will struggle and suffer. His belief runs ahead of proof, matching Morpheus's wager.

affects_outside.enables: The training is now positioned to advance to the jump program (the fear-based test of the next event), which demands exactly the 'the rules are mental' mindset Neo has only just begun to accept.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's belief that possessing knowledge equals mastery is broken, and his trust in Morpheus is strained even as it is reframed; the crew's awe raises the stakes on Neo as the possible One.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The crew (Mouse and 'everyone') who bolt from dinner and watch the fight as entertainment — their collective gasps and disbelief register Neo's breakthrough as a crew-wide event and reinforce the prophecy's momentum off-screen.

events.turns_on: the gap between possessing downloaded knowledge and being able to perform it under pressure

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether the disk Neo reads the label on is the same disk Tank slides into Neo's supplement drive, or a separate one.
Whether Neo ultimately lands a blow in the first exchange — the scene ends mid-exchange with his attacks still being blocked.
What specific combat is taking place inside the programmed reality, and whether Neo's chaotic readings mean he is winning or losing.
Whether Mouse runs out with everyone or stays behind, and who exactly constitutes 'everyone' in the mess hall.
Whether the others besides Mouse react or speak on the main deck, and what specific event on the monitor prompts Mouse's exclamation about neural-kinetics.

events.boundary_reason: The training question begins — 'Can Neo learn to fight?' — with jujitsu loaded (sc-048), escalating through kung fu mastery (sc-049), the first sparring exchange (sc-050), the crew's reactions intercut with the fight (sc-051, sc-052, sc-054, sc-056), Neo being beaten and learning the rules are mental (sc-053), landing his first blow (sc-055), and concluding when Morpheus ends the spar and orders the next stage, the jump program (sc-057). The intercuts to the main deck are the same continuous action, not separate events.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Neo's combat skills are downloaded as a pleasurable shortcut, then immediately submitted to Morpheus's demand for proof. In the sparring program, Neo discovers that possessing the moves is not the same as being able to use them: his furious attacks are effortlessly blocked, his body is dismantled, and he is forced to accept that the simulation's rules are mental and bendable. Under sustained pressure his rage finally unlocks a clean strike that lands on Morpheus, and Morpheus converts the physical breakthrough into a handoff — he is only a guide who can show the door; Neo must step through himself — before ordering the training to advance to the jump program.
prose_before_reconcile.action: download -> demonstration -> sparring -> breakthrough -> handoff
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: the sparring program's bendable rules

events.title: Trinity's Tenderness and Cypher's Scheme
events.summary: Trinity enters Neo's room intending only to leave him dinner, finds him passed out, and—against her stated purpose—lingers over him, pausing with her face close to his and inhaling his scent before slowly pulling away and withdrawing. In the hall she is met by Cypher, who has been watching her emerge and openly probes her attachment; she deflects with a counter that reframes his suspicion as his own problem and leaves without confirming anything, treating him as a manageable nuisance rather than a threat. Cypher reads her guardedness as confirmation of her attachment and treats it as a weakness he can exploit, while separately moving from private resentment toward a concrete plan—suggesting Neo be taken to the Oracle to confirm Morpheus's certainty. The event converts a wordless private feeling into a contested secret held by a skeptical witness, and introduces the Oracle as the proposed mechanism for verifying Morpheus's faith.
events.action: Trinity leaves dinner for Neo and lingers over the passed-out Neo before withdrawing; Cypher, having watched her emerge, intercepts her in the hall, probes her attachment to Neo, and—after she deflects—redirects the conversation toward taking Neo to the Oracle to confirm Morpheus's certainty.

registers.entry: carries a practical, caretaking purpose toward Neo
registers.change: Against her stated purpose, she lingers over the passed-out Neo—pausing with her face close to his, inhaling his scent, then slowly pulling away—before withdrawing.
registers.exit: carries a private, intimate attachment to Neo that she has not acted on but has privately acknowledged

registers.entry: shares with Cypher a crew relationship in which her feelings for Neo are not on the record
registers.change: Cypher observes her emerge from Neo's room and openly probes her attachment; the private feeling becomes something a skeptical crew member is now watching and testing.
registers.exit: her attachment to Neo is a contested secret held by Cypher, who suspects it and is actively testing it

registers.entry: believes Cypher's needling is the usual cynicism, deflatable with a cool deflection
registers.change: She deflects his probe with a counter ('Don't tell me you're a believer now?') and leaves without confirming anything, treating him as a nuisance to be managed rather than a real threat.
registers.exit: treats Cypher as a manageable nuisance, not foreseeing that his skepticism hardens into the betrayal of ev-018

registers.entry: holds her position as Morpheus's loyal second, answering for his timing
registers.change: She reasserts this position by answering with doctrine ('Morpheus will take him when he's ready') rather than anything personal, and leaves on her own terms.
registers.exit: holds her position as Morpheus's loyal second, answering for his timing
registers.unchanged_because: She defends the existing order rather than altering her standing; the scene tests her position but does not change it.

registers.entry: secure within the crew; her private feelings pose no operational exposure
registers.change: Cypher's watching and probing introduces a witness who could expose her attachment and, through it, her judgment; the private becomes a potential liability.
registers.exit: exposed to a skeptical witness whose suspicion could later be turned against her or Neo

state_triples.reading: Trinity believes she is managing a minor nuisance with a cool deflection, when she is actually standing at the first crack of the crew's fracture; she does not yet read Cypher as a threat, and her refusal to put her feelings on the record is both self-protection and the exact thing that lets his suspicion grow unchallenged.

registers.entry: quietly resentful and sidelined, watching the crew's priorities shift toward a candidate he doubts
registers.change: He moves from suspicion to a concrete plan, suggesting Neo be taken to the Oracle to confirm Morpheus's certainty—turning private resentment into an active probe.
registers.exit: actively testing whether Morpheus's faith can be verified, seeding his later position that the prophecy is unproven

registers.entry: suspects Trinity is emotionally compromised by Neo but has no confirmation
registers.change: He observes her emerge from Neo's room and probes her attachment directly; when she deflects rather than denies, he reads her guardedness as confirmation of the attachment.
registers.exit: believes he has confirmed Trinity's attachment to Neo through her deflection, and treats it as a weakness he can exploit

registers.entry: holds a lower, sidelined position in the crew relative to the favored candidate Neo
registers.change: He performs casual indifference and needling to mask the wound of his sidelined position, but does not alter his standing.
registers.exit: holds a lower, sidelined position in the crew relative to the favored candidate Neo
registers.unchanged_because: The scene expresses his resentment but does not change his position within the crew; if anything, his maneuvering entrenches his opposition rather than advancing him.

registers.entry: resentful and skeptical of Morpheus's certainty about Neo
registers.change: He channels that resentment into a strategic question about the Oracle, performing casual indifference so the probe doesn't look like a wound.
registers.exit: resentment now directed into a pragmatic-seeming test of Morpheus's faith, the thin end of the wedge toward his betrayal

registers.entry: his dissent from Morpheus's certainty is private and unexpressed
registers.change: He voices his skepticism about the prophecy through the Oracle probe, moving his dissent from private resentment toward active expression.
registers.exit: his opposition to the crew's faith is now partially exposed and in motion, advancing toward open betrayal

state_triples.reading: Cypher believes he is being a reasonable pragmatist, testing an unverified faith with a sensible question, when he is actually withdrawing loyalty and laying the groundwork for betrayal; his needling masks a wound, and his 'reasonable skepticism' is the thin end of a wedge he does not yet see will become his treason.

affects_outside.enables: The Oracle is now introduced into the story as the mechanism for verifying faith in the One, setting up Morpheus's later decision to take Neo to her; Cypher's suspicion of Trinity's attachment and his skepticism about the prophecy seed the ideological grounds for his betrayal of ev-018.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Trinity's private attachment to Neo is no longer safe; it is now held by a skeptical witness who can exploit it, raising the relational and operational stakes for her and for Neo's standing.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus's certainty about Neo is now subject to a test that a crew member is actively proposing; Cypher's resentment, previously private, has begun moving toward open dissent.

events.turns_on: Trinity's deflection, which Cypher reads as confirmation of her attachment to Neo, and the Oracle as the proposed test of Morpheus's faith in Neo

carried_uncertainty.what: whether Neo is actually asleep or merely pretending during Trinity's intimate moment
whether Trinity's feelings for Neo are romantic or simply protective
whether Cypher's questions are genuine curiosity or a calculated probe of Trinity's feelings

events.boundary_reason: The training concludes and the story shifts to a new thread — the interpersonal and political fallout. Trinity's private moment with the sleeping Neo (sc-063) flows directly into Cypher confronting her in the hall and planting the idea of the Oracle (sc-064). This raises a new question about loyalty and the coming betrayal, separate from the physical training.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Trinity enters Neo's room intending only to leave him dinner, finds him passed out, and—against her stated purpose—lingers over him in a private, intimate moment before withdrawing. Stepping into the hall, she is met by Cypher, who has been watching her emerge; he needles her about the dinner and Neo, then, when she deflects, pivots to a concrete strategic probe—that Morpheus should take Neo to the Oracle, who 'would know.' Trinity refuses to confirm anything, reframes his suspicion as his own problem, and walks away on her own terms. The event converts a wordless private feeling into a contested secret held by a skeptical witness, and introduces the Oracle as the story's mechanism for verifying faith.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Trinity leaves dinner for Neo, lingers over him, then is intercepted by Cypher in the hall, who probes her attachment and redirects the conversation toward taking Neo to the Oracle.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: the Oracle as the proposed test of Morpheus's faith in Neo

events.title: Agent Training and the Sentinel Ambush
events.summary: Morpheus runs Neo through a training program that teaches him Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone still plugged in, whose power is rule-bound while his is not, and who are lethal — every fighter before him died — yet he is cast as the prophesied exception who will succeed where they failed. A Sentinel ambush then forces the Nebuchadnezzar to set down and wedge itself into a supply line too small for the machine; Tank powers the ship down and arms the E.M.P., gripping the red key, while the crew endures the sound-hunting machine gliding over them in frozen silence before it passes. Morpheus does not brief Neo on the Sentinel in the moment, and whether Tank answers his intercom hail is not shown.
events.action: Morpheus teaches Neo the rules of Agents inside a training program; a Sentinel (Squiddy) ambush interrupts and forces the crew to power down, arm the E.M.P., and hide in a supply line too small for the machine.

registers.entry: Neo believes he is inside the real Matrix and is confused when it freezes.
registers.change: Learns he is in a training program, that Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone still plugged in, and that their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not.
registers.exit: Neo knows he is in a training program and that Agents are sentient programs inhabitable by anyone still plugged in, defeatable because their power is rule-bound.

registers.entry: Neo is a struggling trainee, physically out of his depth, bumped and shouldered off the path.
registers.change: Confronted with the lethal stakes of fighting Agents — every fighter before him died — and told he will succeed where they failed.
registers.exit: Neo is under the weight of the lethal stakes of the real war and cast as a prophesied exception who will survive where others died.

registers.entry: Neo begins to angle around Dozer to get a better look.
registers.change: Morpheus grabs him and warns the machine will hear him; Neo freezes.
registers.exit: Neo is frozen and still, obeying Morpheus's command without argument.

registers.entry: Neo trusts Morpheus as a reliable guide whose astonishing claims can be trusted, but only half-believes and leans on authority.
registers.change: Neo's instant freeze on Morpheus's command demonstrates pure, uncomplicated obedience and faith.
registers.exit: Neo's trust in Morpheus is at its peak — pure and unquestioning — the last moment before it can be tested.

state_triples.reading: Neo believes he is an ordinary man being asked to do impossible things, and his self-conception lags far behind what Morpheus and the world expect of him — the gap is the engine of his arc. He also believes Morpheus is in control of every threat, which the Sentinel scene quietly undercuts: Morpheus's composure is evasion, not dominance.

registers.entry: Morpheus has not yet made contact to check on the crew's status.
registers.change: Clicks the intercom and hails Tank, asking how things are going.
registers.exit: Morpheus has opened the intercom channel and posed the question to Tank; whether Tank answers is not shown.

registers.entry: Morpheus is running a training lesson in the program, in command and composed.
registers.change: A Sentinel sweeps in; Morpheus orders Dozer to set the ship down and hide in a supply line.
registers.exit: Morpheus is in active evasion from a Sentinel, treating survival as routine and commanding the crew into stillness.

registers.entry: Morpheus believes Neo can be brought up to speed on real threats later, after the immediate danger passes.
registers.change: The Sentinel ambush leaves no time to teach; Morpheus does not brief Neo on the Squiddy.
registers.exit: Neo remains dangerously uninformed about the Sentinel at the exact moment he needs context — a gap Morpheus does not close.

registers.entry: Morpheus is teaching in the cockpit, composed and in command.
registers.change: Grabs Neo physically to stop him moving, then models total stillness as the machine passes.
registers.exit: Morpheus is the enforcer of silence, using physical restraint rather than speech to keep the untested crew alive.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus carries a fierce, almost messianic certainty that Neo is the One and will succeed where five previous candidates died — a faith, not a fact, that colors his teaching with pressure he will not name. His 'enemy' framing of ordinary people is a teaching tool that flattens the moral complexity he actually holds (they are 'the very people we are trying to save').

registers.entry: The Nebuchadnezzar is moving through the sewer main, trailing a swirling, supercharged, electromagnetic wake.
registers.change: Sets down and maneuvers into a pipe that barely accommodates its size, ending almost wedged into the tight space.
registers.exit: The Nebuchadnezzar is set down, almost wedged into a pipe that barely accommodates its size.

registers.entry: The Nebuchadnezzar is moving through the sewer main, a detectable moving target.
registers.change: A Sentinel sweeps in; the ship is set down and hidden in a supply line too small for the machine.
registers.exit: The Nebuchadnezzar is hidden and powered down, concealed from the Sentinel but trapped in a tight space.

registers.entry: The Nebuchadnezzar is moving through the sewer main.
registers.change: Sets down and is almost wedged into a pipe that barely accommodates its size.
registers.exit: The Nebuchadnezzar is set down, almost wedged into a pipe that barely accommodates its size.

registers.entry: Dozer is flying the ship through the sewer main, first to register the threat.
registers.change: A Sentinel sweeps in; Dozer swears ('Shit') and squeezes the ship into a tiny supply line.
registers.exit: Dozer has executed the evasion, hiding the ship in a line too small for the machine — rattled but competent.

registers.entry: Dozer assumes a newcomer squeezing into the cockpit knows what a Squiddy is.
registers.change: Neo's 'Squiddy?' reveals his ignorance; Dozer delivers a terse briefing ('Search and destroy') under pressure.
registers.exit: Dozer has given Neo his first real briefing on the Sentinel, delivered under pressure rather than by choice.

registers.entry: Dozer is at his station, flying the ship.
registers.change: Squeezes the ship into a tiny supply line, then later reaches to clear frost from the windshield.
registers.exit: Dozer remains at his post as the ship's eyes, unbothered and procedural through the ambush.

registers.entry: Dozer believes the crew is in capable hands and that this is a survivable, ordinary evasion.
registers.change: The machine glides over the ship with 'shark-like malevolence'; the reality is closer than his ease suggests.
registers.exit: Dozer's belief that this is routine holds — the ship survives — but his ease understates the danger and what the moment costs Neo.

registers.entry: Trinity knows what a Sentinel is and that it is a search-and-destroy machine.
registers.change: Neo's 'Squiddy?' reveals his ignorance; Trinity supplies the definition before Dozer's terse add-on.
registers.exit: Trinity has briefed Neo on the Sentinel, establishing herself as the crew's interpreter for the newcomer.

registers.entry: Trinity is in the cockpit during the Sentinel ambush, composed and alert.
registers.change: The crew waits in frozen silence as the machine glides over them; Trinity holds her composure.
registers.exit: Trinity has survived the ambush; the threat is over and she breathes easier with the crew.

registers.entry: Trinity treats Neo as a passenger to be briefed, a variable to be managed on Morpheus's account.
registers.change: She answers his questions directly and completely, watching both the threat and the newcomer.
registers.exit: Trinity has begun treating Neo as someone worth protecting and educating, ahead of the crew's general skepticism.

registers.entry: Trinity is in the cockpit, close enough that Neo must whisper into her ear.
registers.change: She answers Neo's questions while the crew waits in silence; she holds her post through the ambush.
registers.exit: Trinity remains at her post, the crew's interpreter and protector, composed through the danger.

state_triples.reading: Trinity does not yet know that the frightened man whispering questions is the prophecy's object — nothing in this event could tell her. Her coolness now is the distance the coming events will have to close; she already treats him as someone worth protecting and educating, ahead of the crew's general skepticism.

events.boundary_reason: These scenes form one continuous action — Neo's combat training is cut short by Tank's distress call, launching the ship into a real Sentinel attack that runs through the evasion, the E.M.P. arming, the frozen wait, the machine's pass, and the crew finally falling asleep once safe. Cutting between the training program and the ship during this single crisis is one event; it ends when the danger passes and the ship goes quiet.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Morpheus runs Neo through a training program that reclassifies the Matrix's inhabitants as enemies and introduces Agents as lethal, rule-bound programs Neo can surpass — then a Sentinel ambush forces the Nebuchadnezzar to power down and hide in a supply line, where the crew endures a sound-hunting machine in freezing silence before it passes and they finally sleep. The event converts Neo's confusion into the story's real stakes and converts abstract danger into lived, physical survival.

events.title: Cypher's Doubt Hardens into Treason
events.summary: Over a drink on the main deck, Cypher tells Neo that Morpheus has believed he found the One five times before and that all five died taking on an Agent, converting Neo's awe into seeded doubt and subtly distancing him from Morpheus's certainty. Then, meeting Agent Smith in the Matrix at a restaurant table, Cypher commits to an explicit bargain: he will deliver Morpheus — the man who holds the Zion mainframe access codes — in exchange for being reinserted into the Matrix. The crew's internal doubt is now an active, named betrayal with a specific target.
events.action: Cypher isolates Neo over drinks and reveals that five of Morpheus's predecessors died taking on an Agent, reframing Neo's destiny as a deadly pattern rather than a singular calling; then, at a restaurant table inside the Matrix, Cypher finalises a deal with Agent Smith to hand over Morpheus in return for reinsertion, and Smith names Morpheus as the target through whom he will obtain the Zion mainframe access codes.

events.title: Departure for the Oracle
events.summary: Morpheus breaks the crew's ordinary mess-hall routine to take Neo, and only Neo, to see the Oracle. The crew jacks in and materializes at the Hotel Lafayette; Cypher, acting alone against them, drops a live cellular phone into an alley garbage can to connect a line, then drives the group into the city, where Neo confronts the falseness of his own memories and Trinity is struck physically mute at the point of revealing what she was told about him. The event moves the crew from ship to Matrix under a false premise of safety, with a tracking line now live behind them.
events.action: The crew eats a gray protein breakfast in the mess hall, trading jokes about the machines' inability to replicate real food, until Morpheus enters, orders twelve-hour standby, and announces he is taking Neo to see 'her.' Tank supplies the name Neo lacks: the Oracle. The crew straps into their chairs on the main deck and Tank strikes the enter key, initiating the flight. They materialize in the empty Hotel Lafayette room as a phone rings; Morpheus answers and confirms 'We're in.' Neo steps back into the Matrix for the first time since his release, squinting at the harsh sun as the only one without sunglasses. Cypher drops a live cellular phone into a garbage can in the alley, its blue display lighting as the line connects, while the others move toward a car. In the car, Neo confesses that his lifelong memories never really happened; Trinity tells him the Matrix cannot tell him who he is and that only the Oracle can. When Neo presses her on what the Oracle told her about him, she goes physically mute and breathless. The car stops; Morpheus takes Neo out, and Cypher needles Trinity in the rearview mirror with a knowing smile.
