prose_before_reconcile.summary: Morpheus breaks the crew's ordinary mess-hall routine to take Neo, and only Neo, to see the Oracle. The crew jacks in and materializes at the Hotel Lafayette; Cypher, already bargaining with the enemy, plants a live cellular phone in an alley garbage can to connect a line against them, then drives the group into the city where Neo confronts the falseness of his own memories and the Oracle's power to name identity, and Trinity is struck physically mute at the point of revealing what she was told about him. The event moves the crew from ship to Matrix under a false premise of safety, with a tracking line now live behind them.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The crew eats a gray protein breakfast in the mess hall, trading jokes about the machines' inability to replicate real food, until Morpheus enters, orders twelve-hour standby, and announces he is taking Neo to see 'her.' Tank supplies the name Neo lacks: the Oracle. The crew straps into their chairs on the main deck and Tank strikes the enter key, initiating the flight. They materialize in the empty Hotel Lafayette room as a phone rings; Morpheus answers and confirms 'We're in.' Neo steps back into the Matrix for the first time since his release, squinting at the harsh sun as the only one without sunglasses. Cypher drops a live cellular phone into a garbage can in the alley, its blue display lighting as the line connects, while the others move toward a car. In the car, Neo confesses that his lifelong memories never really happened; Trinity tells him the Matrix cannot tell him who he is and that only the Oracle can. When Neo presses her on what the Oracle told her about him, she goes physically mute and breathless. The car jerks to a stop; Morpheus takes Neo out, and Cypher needles Trinity in the rearview mirror with a knowing smile.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The live cellular phone Cypher drops into the garbage can, whose connecting line turns an ordinary departure into a tracked one.

events.title: The Oracle's Verdict
events.summary: The Oracle tells Neo he is not the One but has 'the gift' and is 'waiting for something,' then delivers a binding prophecy: Morpheus's faith is so absolute he will sacrifice his life to save Neo's, and Neo himself will hold the choice of which of them dies. Neo is frightened to somatic panic, then physically calmed exactly as the Oracle promised, while carrying the lethal decision he can no longer shrug off as Morpheus's private burden. Neo is escorted from the kitchen into the sitting room, where Morpheus — alone with him after the priestess leaves — tells him he need not report what was said because it was said for him alone, and offers to keep its contents secret; Neo accepts that trust.
events.action: The Oracle engineers the breaking of a vase to demonstrate that choice, not fate, governs action; examines Neo; tells him he has 'the gift' but is 'waiting for something,' perhaps his next life; then states that Morpheus's faith is so absolute he will sacrifice his own life to save Neo's and that Neo himself will hold the choice of which of them dies. She reassures him he controls his own life and that a cookie will settle him, and the tightness in his chest fades exactly as promised. Neo is then escorted by the priestess out of the kitchen into the sitting room, where Morpheus — alone with him after the priestess leaves — places a hand on his shoulder and tells him he need not report what was said to anyone because it was said for him alone; Neo nods and eats his cookie.

events.turns_on: The event turns on the Oracle's prophecy — that Morpheus will die to save Neo and that Neo will choose which of them lives — landing as a binding, personal decision Neo can no longer disbelieve his way out of; on the demonstration that choice, not fate, governs action (the vase) and on the Oracle's visible, fulfilled promise to calm him; and on Morpheus's refusal to demand the verdict, instead releasing Neo from any obligation to report it and offering to keep its contents secret — the very self-sacrificing faith the Oracle has just named as fatal.

events.title: Exit to the Real World
events.summary: The crew leaves the Oracle's building and travels by car to the city street, then enters the Hotel Lafayette, arriving on the threshold of the exit to the Real World. Neo practices the cover story 'Right as rain,' reassuring the crew while privately carrying the verdict alone; Trinity asks if he is all right and accepts the cover without forcing it. Cypher probes for the verdict with 'good news or bad news?' and is shut down by Morpheus's 'Not now, Cypher,' leaving him aware he is being excluded from a truth the others share, his resentment suppressed but stored. Tank relays 'They're on their way,' putting the crew in motion toward the extraction. The secret is sealed within the group; the crew arrives at the Hotel Lafayette preparing to exit.

events.title: The Trap Is Revealed
events.summary: Neo notices a black cat and then a second identical one, dismisses the repeat as nothing, then names it a 'deja vu.' Trinity stops him, interrogates him, and translates the sign: a deja vu is usually a glitch in the Matrix that happens when 'they change something.' Tank, at the operator's station, sees his monitors seize, traces what was changed, and identifies it as a deliberate ambush, shouting the warning. Trinity converts the glitch into a threat-assessment — the Matrix is being rewritten, Agents are close — while listening with Morpheus to the growing sound of helicopter blades. Morpheus, silent, locates the threat at the layer of the building itself. The crew's unalarmed advance up the stairwell is arrested; the party is left exposed in the open with a confirmed, closing threat.
events.action: recognition-and-diagnosis of a Matrix rewrite as a deliberate ambush

registers.entry: Notices a black cat and a second identical one without understanding their significance, treating the repeat as an ordinary coincidence.
registers.change: Names the repeat 'deja vu,' then is told by Trinity that a deja vu is usually a glitch in the Matrix that happens when 'they change something.'
registers.exit: Understands the repeated cat is a glitch signalling that the Matrix is being actively altered, and that his throwaway observation has become significant — he admits he is out of his depth ('What is it?').

registers.entry: A passenger being moved up the stairwell, unalarmed.
registers.change: His casual remark stops the others dead; he is repositioned from a companion to the source of an alarm that forces the adults into threat-assessment, then into a civilian being briefed under fire.
registers.exit: The one who has inadvertently sprung the tripwire and must now be told what is happening — his role shifts from follower to the person whose observation has put the crew on alert.

registers.entry: Moving up the stairwell with the crew, unalarmed.
registers.change: The recognition of the glitch, followed by the sound of approaching helicopter blades, ends the unalarmed advance.
registers.exit: Exposed in the open stairwell with an approaching threat, safety no longer assumed.

registers.entry: Casual, dismissing the repeat as nothing.
registers.change: Reads how seriously the others take it; moves from deflection ('Nothing. Just had a little deja vu') through a hedged answer to an exposed question.
registers.exit: Alarmed and recalibrating — no longer pretending, admitting he does not know the rules of this world.

registers.entry: A newcomer among the crew, not yet reading the Matrix as they do.
registers.change: Trinity interrogates him and translates reality for him; he begins reading the adults' reactions and adjusting to them.
registers.exit: Being treated as someone who must be briefed under pressure — the crew's most junior member, whose civilian reflexes have just been exposed.

registers.change: None recorded — he remains on the stairwell through the event.
registers.exit: On the stairwell of the Hotel Lafayette with the crew.
registers.unchanged_because: No scene records Neo leaving or changing position on the stairwell; the event turns on what he perceives and is told, not on where he moves.

state_triples.reading: Neo believes he has startled Trinity with a harmless coincidence and that her intensity is disproportionate — the last civilian misreading he makes before the helicopters prove her right. Beneath that, he feels a jolt of recognition that this world runs on rules he does not yet know, and that his throwaway line has just become operational. He conceals his embarrassment behind dismissal, then lets it drop to admit he is out of his depth.

registers.entry: Typing rapidly at the operator's station, focused on his work.
registers.change: Notices something on his screens ('What is that...?'), then the monitors glitch as though the Matrix had an electronic seizure, and he traces the alteration — 'sees what was changed' — and identifies it as a deliberate ambush.
registers.exit: Knows the situation is a trap ('It's a trap!') — he has read the rewrite of the Matrix and named its intent.

registers.entry: Focused, absorbed in typing.
registers.change: Interrupted by an anomaly, then alarmed by the monitor seizure, then alarmed recognition as he identifies the ambush.
registers.exit: Alarmed and shouting a warning — repeated exclamations ('Oh shit!') escalating to a shouted declaration ('It's a trap!').

registers.entry: At the operator's station on the main deck.
registers.change: None recorded — he remains at the station through the event.
registers.exit: At the operator's station on the main deck.
registers.unchanged_because: No scene records Tank leaving the operator's station; the event turns on what he sees and concludes, not on where he moves.

registers.entry: The operator monitoring the Matrix from the ship, doing routine work.
registers.change: Becomes the first to diagnose the situation as a deliberate ambush, shifting him from a passive monitor to the one who sounds the alarm for the crew in the Matrix.
registers.exit: The crew member who has identified the trap and is raising it — the diagnostic authority in this moment.

registers.entry: Safe aboard the ship, physically removed from the Matrix.
registers.change: None recorded — his body is not in danger; only his read of the situation changes.
registers.exit: Safe aboard the ship, physically removed from the Matrix.
registers.unchanged_because: Tank's body remains on the ship throughout; the threat he identifies is to the crew inside the Matrix, not to himself.

registers.exit: A crew member connected to those in the Matrix through his monitoring role.
registers.unchanged_because: No scene records a change in how Tank relates to the others; he does his job as operator, and his warning flows through an existing crew bond.

state_triples.reading: Tank does not yet know who set the trap or why; he only knows the Matrix has been deliberately rewritten around the crew. His alarm is that of the operator who sees the board change and recognises intent — he is reading a hostile hand, not a random fault.

registers.entry: Alert, interrogating Neo about his remark, still investigating the cat.

state_triples.reading: Trinity believes she must translate reality for Neo because he is too new to understand — a belief the raid will disprove as he begins to act on instinct. She also assumes Morpheus is listening for the same threat and will give the same read, settling the situation between them with a look; but Morpheus is tuned to the building's breath, a layer she does not register, so their agreement here is partly her assumption. Her interrogation is not curiosity — it is triage, and she lets her own explanation to Neo double as her confirmation.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus believes Neo is the one to be protected and guided toward his destiny, worth any risk to the crew — a conviction freshly reinforced by the Oracle. That private certainty is what will soon force the choice the Oracle named and lead to his own capture; the certainty that shields Neo does not shield Morpheus. He says nothing because he does not need to perform certainty — his silence is the most senior person in the room working.

affects_outside.enables: The confirmed glitch and Tank's 'It's a trap!' set the crew onto a defensive, evasive footing — the raid that follows (the Agents closing on the exposed party in the stairwell) is now inevitable rather than merely possible. Neo's first act of reading the Matrix like a freed mind begins his shift from passenger to operative. Tank's identification of a deliberate ambush raises the question of who inside the crew set it, which will drive the betrayal plot.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The crew's unalarmed, covert movement through the Matrix is spent — they are now exposed and being hunted. Neo's civilian reflexes (dismissing the anomaly) are exhausted as a viable way of operating in this world.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Agents / the machines: the deja vu signals that 'they' are changing the Matrix — the hostile force is now actively rewriting the world around the crew, an off-screen action this event registers but does not show.

events.turns_on: Neo's naming of the repeated black cat as a 'deja vu' — a Matrix glitch signalling the simulation is being actively altered

carried_uncertainty.what: What exactly Tank saw on his screens in sc-090 that made him ask 'What is that...?' — the scene flags it as undetermined.
Whether Cypher responds or reacts to Tank's question in sc-090 — the scene leaves it open.

Whether the second black cat was truly identical to the first — Neo himself hedges ('It might have been. I'm not sure'), so the event cannot assert the repeat as a confirmed fact, only as the crew's working read.

Whether Morpheus and Trinity share the same read of the threat — Trinity assumes their wordless look settles it, but the scene isolates Morpheus listening to the building's breath, a layer she does not register, so their agreement is not confirmed.
Who changed the Matrix and set the trap — Tank identifies it as a deliberate ambush but the scenes do not reveal the saboteur.

events.boundary_reason: Cross-cutting between the crew ascending the hotel and Tank on the main deck, this is one continuous action: the deja-vu glitch, the monitors seizing, Trinity's explanation, and Tank's 'It's a trap!' all converge on a single realization. It ends once the ambush is confirmed on both sides; the next scene shifts to arming up and the physical escape under threat.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: A repeated black cat triggers Neo's recognition of a deja vu, which the crew reads as a Matrix glitch — the signal that the simulation is being rewritten around them — while Tank, monitoring from the main deck, traces the alteration and names it for what it is: a deliberate ambush. The event converts an eerie coincidence into a confirmed, closing threat, with helicopter blades audibly approaching the exposed party in the stairwell.
prose_before_reconcile.action: recognition-and-diagnosis of an ambush already sprung inside the Matrix
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: the deja vu (repeated black cat) as a Matrix glitch

events.title: The Ambush Springs (Mouse's Death)
events.summary: The Matrix glitch the crew had dismissed snaps shut into a coordinated trap. As the helicopter arrives overhead, Apoc slaps a gun into Neo's hand and treats him as one who must pull his own weight, while Morpheus drives the group up the staircase. In the basement an unidentified person severs the building's main phone cable with bolt cutters, cutting the hardline escape route. In Room 1313 the windows are rewritten into solid brick and combat boots explode into the room. Tank, having declared the trap from the main deck, sees the line cut and transmits a warning to Mouse, racing to reach him in time — but by the time the call connects the windows are already bricked and the exit is gone. Mouse, warned that the line is cut and it is a trap, finds the window exit erased and is cornered; he is thrown backwards as bullets slam him against the bricked window and is gunned down. Morpheus halts on the stairs, arrested by the sound of Mouse's scream swallowed by gunfire. Tank is reduced to watching helplessly, unable to intervene. Mouse dies in the Matrix — the first crew death of the trap — and on the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck his real body convulses and dies, the flatline alarm sounding.
events.action: The crew reacts to the arrival of the threat by arming Neo and moving up the staircase under Morpheus's command; the trap is sprung when an unidentified person severs the main phone cable in the basement and Room 1313's windows are rewritten into solid brick; Mouse is isolated, cornered, and killed against the bricked window; and Tank witnesses his death helplessly from the ship while Morpheus is arrested on the stairs by the sound of the gunfire.

affects_outside.enables: The trap's springing forces the crew into open combat and flight, ending the prophecy-and-dread phase that began at the Oracle and launching the chase sequence that follows. Mouse's death — the first crew casualty — raises the stakes of the Oracle's 'not the One' verdict and demonstrates that the Matrix environment itself can be rewritten as a weapon, a rule that governs every later engagement.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The crew loses Mouse, its youngest member, and loses the building's hardline as an escape route, forcing them to find another way out under fire. Tank and Morpheus are reduced to helpless witnesses, spending the crew's ability to intervene.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Tank and Morpheus, aboard the Nebuchadnezzar and on the stairs respectively, are left witnessing Mouse's death with no power to prevent it — a position that worsens for them and will shape their choices in the pursuit that follows.

events.turns_on: The hardline escape route and the editable room wall are the pivots of this event. The main phone cable is severed in the basement by an unidentified person, and Room 1313's windows are rewritten into solid brick, so the two things the crew would rely on to escape — the phone line and the window exit — are both destroyed before Tank's warning can reach Mouse. Mouse's belief that the room's layout is stable and that an exit remains open is exactly what kills him. These are recorded as entities with state triples below.

carried_uncertainty.what: The identity and allegiance of the person who cuts the hardline in the basement.
Whether the cable-cutting is an ally or enemy action, and why the cable is being cut.
Exactly who the combat BOOT-wearing intruders are.
What Tank is watching on the main deck and whether anyone else is present with him.
Whether Morpheus survives the engagement on the stairs, and Mouse's fate beyond the gunfire heard.
Whether anyone else is present on the main deck when Mouse's real body dies.

events.boundary_reason: This run is the trap executing: Neo is armed, the hardline is cut, Mouse is cornered and gunned down, intercut with Tank and Morpheus's helpless reactions to the killing. It closes once Mouse is dead (flatline), which ends the 'trap closing' unit and pivots to the survivors' escape problem.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: The Matrix glitch the crew dismissed as a minor error snaps shut into a coordinated trap. As the helicopter arrives overhead, the crew arms up and moves to escape, while an unseen hand severs the building's hardline and rewrites Room 1313 so its windows become solid brick. Mouse, warned by Tank that the line is cut and it is a trap, discovers the exit has been erased and is cornered by the intruders. Morpheus, still on the stairs, is halted by the sound of Mouse's scream being swallowed by gunfire. Mouse is gunned down against the bricked window and, on the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, his real body convulses once and dies, the flatline alarm sounding.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The crew reacts to the arrival of the threat by arming and moving, the trap is sprung by cutting the hardline and rewriting the room's windows into brick, Mouse is isolated and killed, and the crew's operators witness his death helplessly from the ship.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The hardline escape route and the editable room wall are the pivots of this event. The main phone cable is severed in the basement, and Room 1313's windows are rewritten into solid brick, so the two things the crew would rely on to escape — the phone line and the window exit — are both destroyed. These are recorded as entities with state triples below.

events.title: The Police Sweep / Tank Finds the Wet-Wall
events.summary: The police arrive at the Hotel Lafayette poised to search it and convert their building-level cordon into an active interior clearance, dispersing through the floors with flashlights probing the rotting darkness floor by floor. On the ship, Tank, tasked with finding a structural drawing fast, locates it and delivers it instantly, then pulls the main wet-wall schematic Morpheus demands next, confirming himself as the crew's remote eyes feeding schematics one step ahead. Morpheus, awaiting the drawing, receives it and immediately directs the relay toward the main wet-wall.

events.title: The Agents Converge on the Eighth Floor
events.summary: Having killed Mouse in Room 1313, Agent Smith treats the phone line clicking dead in his ear not as a failed connection but as the signal that the trap has closed, and turns that disconnection into the coordinate — the eighth floor — that summons the converging Agents and police. Boots clatter up the marble staircase and cops flood the hall and rush everywhere on the eighth floor, deploying across it as an overwhelming, impersonal force. Agent Brown listens to his earpiece, receiving the relayed information. Meanwhile Morpheus, guided remotely by Tank's authoritative directions, is led to a spot directly in front of him on that same eighth floor — walking calmly into the trap he believes is leading him out.

events.title: The Fugitives Vanish Into the Walls
events.summary: The escapees pass through the man-sized hole in the Room 808 wall into the main plumbing wall and descend along the grease-black stack pipes, concealing themselves and leaving only the breach behind. Cops sweeping the now-empty room come upon that hole and learn the fugitives escaped by breaking through the wall, but hold no more than the breach as evidence of their route. In the hall, Agent Brown stands over Morpheus's abandoned jacket and demands the fugitives' location, commanding a search that has lost its live target and been reduced to interrogating the empty trail.
events.action: The escapees enter the plumbing wall through the hole and worm downward along the stack pipes, passing from exposed occupants of Room 808 into concealment below their point of entry, unknown to the pursuers. Cops sweeping the room come upon the man-sized hole smashed through the plaster and lath in the bathroom and become aware the fugitives escaped by breaking through the wall. Agent Brown, standing over Morpheus's jacket, shifts from examining the trace to openly demanding where the fugitives are.

events.title: Ambush in the Walls; Morpheus Sacrifices Himself
events.summary: A cop searching ROOM 608 isolates a strange sound and, pressing his ear to the plaster, is exposed when the wall bulges and shatter-cracks to reveal the crew hidden inside; gunfire erupts as the crew returns fire from the wall, and an Agent breaks through to strangle Neo until Morpheus dives on it, pins it before it reaches its weapon, and commands Trinity to get Neo out as 'all that matters,' sacrificing his own escape so the others can flee.
events.action: Searching ROOM 608 in silence, one cop isolates a strange sound near the bathroom the others have not noted and presses his ear to the thin plaster membrane. The wall bulges and shatter-cracks, exposing the occupants dangerously close and about to break through. Gunfire begins: the cop spins out of the bathroom for cover, while inside the wall Neo finds his gun first and blasts wildly through the plaster and lath, and Trinity pulls Cypher free from the line of fire. As the cop is about to whirl back in, something seizes him; his body spasms and his M-16 falls, leaving him frozen and disarmed. Two arms smash through the wall and throw Neo against the iron stack pipe, fingers gouging his neck as he is strangled. Morpheus explodes through the plaster and lath, dives on Agent Smith, and pins it before it can reach its weapon; the two crash to the wet terrazzo floor. Morpheus orders Trinity to get Neo out as 'all that matters,' escalating from request to command. Trinity scrambles up past Cypher toward Morpheus calling his name, balls her fists in frustration when overruled, then relays 'Go!' to Apoc and drags the protesting Neo down the inside of the wall, taking up the charge of Neo's survival while Neo witnesses Morpheus sacrificing himself and cries out against it.

prose_before_reconcile.action: The crew is concealed inside the plumbing walls between rooms when a cop, alerted by a strange sound, presses his ear to the plaster and hears whispers, hisses and a grunt. The wall bulges and shatter-cracks, revealing the fugitives to the cop. The cop opens fire into the wall; Trinity pulls Cypher clear while Neo arms himself and blasts back through the plaster. One cop, retreating for cover, is seized mid-movement, his body spasming and his weapon dropping. Inside the wall, two arms smash through and an Agent begins to strangle Neo; Morpheus dives through the plaster, pins the Agent before it can reach its weapon, and orders Trinity to get Neo out because 'he is all that matters.' Trinity, though anguished, relays the order and drags the protesting Neo down the inside of the wall to escape, leaving Morpheus holding the Agent.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The plumbing wall — the plaster-and-lath membrane separating the hidden crew from ROOM 608 — which first conceals the fugitives and then betrays them when it bulges and shatter-cracks under gunfire, exposing their location and turning a hidden retreat into an open firefight; it is also the barrier Morpheus and the Agent break through to reach each other.

events.title: Morpheus Is Captured
events.summary: In Room 608, Morpheus has already committed to getting Neo out and given the order that removed the only thing he was fighting to protect, so this fight is about buying time and dying on his feet rather than survival. He starts dominant, pinning Agent Smith to the floor in a strangling death grip and taunting him as interchangeable, but Smith pries his hands off, head-butts him three times, and kicks him deep into the wall through plaster and lathe. On Smith's order the cops rush in and bury Morpheus under their numbers, converting the one-on-one fight into a controlled police action: Morpheus is taken alive on Smith's command, becoming a captured prize that turns the crew's escape into a capture-and-rescue problem. On the main deck, Tank reaches toward the screen as if reaching for Morpheus and cries out in distress, registering that the escape has turned into a loss.

events.title: Regroup on the Street
events.summary: Across two channels the scattered crew converges on a shared operational picture: Morpheus is alive but being moved to an unknown location, and an exit is secured at Franklin and Erie. The exit has been routed through Cypher, who has used a faked accident to clear his way out and is now poised to leave, privately elated, while the rest of the crew remains unaware.
events.action: Trinity climbs out from beneath a cracked manhole cover onto the street. On the ship, Tank answers a call and, recognizing the voice, opens an exit at Franklin and Erie for Cypher, who reports a car crash beside a burning paddy wagon and is routed there before hanging up composed and self-satisfied. Trinity and Neo then link up with Tank over the radio: Trinity learns from Tank that Morpheus is alive but being moved to an unknown location and that Cypher is already at Franklin and Erie, the man the crew already suspects; Neo hears that Morpheus is alive, and the fact tightens his sense of inevitability rather than relieving him.

events.title: Cypher's Betrayal
events.summary: Cypher reaches the ship ahead of the returning crew, arms himself at the operator station, shoots the operator Tank twice and leaves him for dead, then murders the still-jacked-in crewmates Apoc and Switch and reveals he has handed Morpheus's location to the Agents. Dozer witnesses the shooting and cries out, so the betrayal is no longer private. Trinity, reaching the exit phone with Neo, is deceived into believing Cypher is a surviving crewmate reporting that Tank 'had an accident,' then learns he killed the crew and gave up Morpheus; the line is severed, stranding her and Neo inside. Cypher is interrupted at the moment of his final kill by Tank, who survived, seized the lightning gun, and fired on him — and that same shot spares Neo, whom Cypher was testing, leaving Cypher blown off his feet and his control of the deck broken.

events.title: The Agents Take Morpheus Into Custody
events.summary: Agent Jones arrives by helicopter at a government highrise with Marines to secure the prisoner, disembarks onto the roof, breaches the roof access, and moves into the building's top-floor maintenance level, advancing toward the executive office. In that office, Morpheus is already held captive—handcuffed to a chair, stripped to the waist, wired to monitors—while Agent Smith, presiding from the window, philosophizes about the Matrix's redesign as the machines' victory. Smith sits directly in front of Morpheus, forces eye contact, and orders the dosage escalated; Agent Brown jams the needle into Morpheus's shoulder and plunges the doubled dose into him, driving his life signs into violent reaction. Smith reframes the torture as inevitable evolution and declares the future belongs to the machines. Jones interrupts the interrogation with an unsolicited warning that a problem is developing—one he has detected before the others register it.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Agent Jones arrives by helicopter at a government highrise with Marines, breaches the roof, and moves into the building to secure the prisoner. In the executive office, Morpheus is already held captive—handcuffed to a chair, stripped to the waist, wired to monitors—while Agent Smith philosophizes about the Matrix's redesign as the machines' victory. Agent Brown injects Morpheus with serum that drives his life signs into violent reaction, and on Smith's order doubles the dosage. Smith reframes the torture as inevitable evolution and declares the future belongs to the machines. Agent Jones enters to warn that a problem is developing, interrupting the interrogation.

prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Morpheus's refusal to break under the doubled dosage — the event pivots on whether the serum forces him to surrender the information, and his fixed, unreadable gaze against the violent reaction of the monitors signals that Smith's assumption of imminent capitulation is about to fail.

events.title: Mourning Morpheus and the Decision to Rescue Him
events.summary: Freshly gutted by Dozer's death, the Nebuchadnezzar crew confront the fact that the Agents are breaking Morpheus's mind to extract Zion's mainframe codes. Tank channels his grief into a clinical case that the only answer is to unplug Morpheus before he breaks, reaching for the plug himself until Trinity, as ranking officer, overrules him and orders him to load Neo and herself up. Trinity flares into rage at Cypher's betrayal, kicking his corpse, then into protest against Tank's plan; when Neo renounces being the One, her private faith in the prophecy cracks and she converts grief into command. Neo, understanding the stakes, rejects the forced choice, declares he is 'just another guy' willing to die for Morpheus, and commits to going into the Matrix to bring him back, trying to forbid Trinity from coming. Morpheus, unconscious and inert, is on the verge of cracking, his alpha pattern shifting from chaotic to ordered as his body fails. The Agents, having concluded their man is dead either way, abandon the interrogation: Jones collapses Brown's hedging into certainty, and Smith reasserts machine control, ordering the sentinels deployed to hunt the ship physically.
events.action: The event turns on the crew's refusal to accept the 'no other choice' that both Tank and the Agents have settled on. The pivots are Neo's rejection of the false binary and his commitment to the rescue, and Trinity's seizure of command after her faith in the prophecy collapses.

events.title: Smith's Interrogation Deepens
events.summary: Agent Smith, having interrogated Morpheus, voices his conviction that humanity is a disease and the Agents its cure, then—angered and disgusted by the failing serum and his own sense of contamination—dismisses Brown and Jones, drops his earphone to sever the Agent channel, and sits beside Morpheus to torture him under a death-or-codes ultimatum. Morpheus, bound and being physically assaulted, sneers through the pain and gives nothing. Brown and Jones, having registered Smith's aberrant anger, are ordered out and leave. Simultaneously, in the construct and aboard the ship, Neo—having confessed to Trinity that he is 'just another guy'—demands guns, arms himself, and jacks into the Matrix with Trinity to begin the rescue; Tank loads their weapons and sends them in.
events.action: The event runs on two fronts. In the interrogation, Smith moves from procedure to ideology to private desperation: he pronounces his disease/cure framework, loses composure as the serum fails, conceals his anger, orders Brown and Jones out, drops his earphone to cut the collective, and escalates to physical torture and an explicit death threat to force out the Zion codes. Morpheus endures, sneering and unbroken. On the second front, Neo converts his crisis of faith into forward motion: he names the need for weapons, arms himself with a hard certainty that the unprecedented raid is its own advantage, and—joined by Trinity, who answers with awe rather than objection—jacks into the Matrix, Tank having loaded the arms and sent them in. The two fronts are set on a collision course, with Morpheus's survival hanging on which reaches its objective first.

events.turns_on: The event turns on Smith's belief that Morpheus holds the Zion codes and can be broken into yielding them, which makes the captivity lethal and time-sensitive and drives the rescue. It also turns on the failing serum, whose failure is what pushes Smith from procedure into personal desperation—his anger, his disgust at feeling 'infected,' and his decision to break from the Agent collective to pursue the codes as his own means of escape. On the rescue front it turns on Neo's self-doubt: he arms as a mortal who does not believe he is the One, yet reframes the unprecedented nature of the raid as the reason it will work.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: While Morpheus is held captive, Agent Smith articulates his ideological conviction that humanity is a disease and the Agents its cure, then—frustrated by the failing serum and disgusted by his own contamination—drives the other Agents away to pursue the Zion codes as his private means of escape. Simultaneously, in the construct and aboard the ship, Neo converts his crisis of faith into a concrete rescue plan, arms himself, and jacks in with Trinity, moving from self-doubt to a hard certainty that the unprecedented nature of the raid is precisely what will make it work.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The event is a two-front pivot. On one side, the interrogation escalates from procedure to ideology and then to personal desperation: Smith reframes the torture as a verdict, isolates himself from the Agent collective, and threatens Morpheus with death to force out Zion's codes. On the other side, the rescue force commits and mobilizes: Neo demands weapons, arms himself with mounting conviction, and—joined by Trinity—jacks into the Matrix to begin the assault. The two fronts are set on a collision course, with Morpheus's survival hanging on which reaches its objective first.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The event turns on Morpheus's mind as 'the key'—Smith's belief that the captive holds the Zion codes and can be broken into yielding them—which is what makes his captivity lethal and time-sensitive and what forces Neo's rescue. It also turns on the failing serum, whose failure is what drives Smith from procedure to personal desperation.

events.title: The Assault on the Government Building
events.summary: Neo and Trinity enter the government building's lobby under the pretense of a routine security check, then reveal weapon-laden harnesses and open fire, massacring the security detail before the soldiers sent as backup can contain them. They fight across the lobby to the elevators; Trinity wires a bomb inside one car while Neo stops it and cuts the cable, and both climb the shaft as the car falls and detonates at the bottom, blowing the elevator bank apart. Above, in an executive office, the three Agents — who have just released the still-captive Morpheus — register the intrusion: Brown demands answers and is told he does not know what is happening, Jones identifies the attack as a rescue attempt, and Smith receives an earphone report that visibly shocks him, shifting the Agents from interrogators to the reactive party.
events.action: Neo and Trinity cross the lobby under the guise of a compliant security check, set off the metal detector on their own beats, then reveal concealed arsenals and kill the guards with precision before the reinforcing soldiers can establish a defense. They advance across the lobby without breaking stride; Trinity drops to wire a plastique-and-napalm bomb in one elevator while Neo stops the car and opens access to the shaft. Neo clamps onto the cable, cuts it below their position, and both climb the shaft as the empty car falls and explodes at the bottom, blowing the doors open and filling the elevator section with fire. Meanwhile the Agents converge on Smith, who has released Morpheus; Jones names the assault a rescue attempt, Brown is repositioned as the least-informed agent, and Smith's earphone report leaves him shaken.

affects_outside.enables: The Agents' shift from interrogators to the reactive party, and specifically Smith's earphone shock, sets up the imminent rescue of Morpheus (ev-028) — the building's security and the Agents' control are now demonstrably breachable. Neo and Trinity's position high in the shaft with a prepared bomb places them to continue the ascent toward the executive office where Morpheus is held.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The government building's lobby security is destroyed and its elevator bank blown apart, spending the element of surprise and committing the rescue to open, escalating combat. The Agents have lost the initiative and the illusion of unbreachable control.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The wider system/Matrix response to a coordinated assault on a government building is now triggered but not shown; the earphone report that shocks Smith implies a larger alarm spreading beyond the office.

events.turns_on: The Assault on the Government Building turns on the Agents' dawning awareness that the intrusion is a rescue — crystallised in Jones's identification of the attack as a rescue attempt and, above all, in the earphone report that visibly shocks Smith and shatters his belief that he is one step ahead. That report is the pivot that transfers momentum from the Agents' control to the rescuers' initiative, while Brown is demoted from accuser to the one left out of the loop.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether the reinforcing soldiers are defeated or merely held off — the lobby firefight ends before it resolves.
Whether Neo and Trinity's objective in the building is specifically to rescue Morpheus — the lobby scene itself does not state their goal (though the surrounding event chain establishes it).
What exactly Smith is hearing over the earphone — the content of the report is not disclosed.
Whether the agents' arrival in the office is a rescue of Smith or a reprimand for what he was doing — the scene does not settle it.
Whether anyone is inside or near the elevator at the moment of its explosion — the lobby scene names no people.

events.boundary_reason: Neo and Trinity's infiltration erupts into open combat and their ascent through the shaft, a single continuous action intercut with the building's reaction.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Acting on the decision to rescue Morpheus, Neo and Trinity storm the government building's lobby, gun down the security detail and the soldiers sent to reinforce it, and fight their way to the elevators. While they rig an explosive in one lift and cut its cable to ride the shaft upward, the elevator they vacated plummets and detonates at the bottom, blowing the lobby's elevator bank apart. In an executive office above, the three Agents — who have just released the still-captive Morpheus — register the intrusion: Brown wants answers, Jones realises a rescue is underway, and Smith receives an earphone report that visibly shocks him, shifting the Agents from interrogators to the reactive party.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Neo and Trinity breach the lobby under cover of a routine security check, reveal concealed weapons, and kill the guards and reinforcing soldiers in a sustained firefight, crossing the lobby without breaking stride. They enter an elevator, where Trinity wires a plastique-and-napalm bomb and Neo stops the car and opens access to the shaft. Neo clamps onto the cable, shoots it below their position, and the falling elevator yanks them up the shaft. The empty car then explodes at the bottom, blowing the elevator doors open and filling the lobby's elevator section with fire. Meanwhile the Agents converge on Smith, who has released Morpheus; Jones identifies the attack as a rescue attempt, and Smith's earphone report leaves him shaken.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The Assault on the Government Building turns on the Agents' dawning awareness that the intrusion is a rescue — crystallised in Jones's 'I think they're trying to save him' and, above all, in the earphone report that visibly shocks Smith. That report is the pivot that transfers momentum from the Agents' control to the rescuers' initiative.

events.title: The Agents Mobilize to Hunt the Intruders
events.summary: Fire alarms, explosions, and triggered sprinklers reach the executive office, cracking Agent Smith's composed, analytical interpretation of the intruders into open personal fury — he experiences the escalation as an insult to the system he embodies and smashes a table. From that fury he issues an absolute command — 'Find them and destroy them!' — converting the pursuit from containment to a kill order, believing he is issuing a controlled directive while the violence of it betrays how personal the escalation has become. Agent Brown, the diagnostician of the three, reaches certainty before any order is given: recognizing the pattern — 'They are actually attacking' — he moves from suspicion to being the first Agent certain the intrusion has become open assault, correcting his own prior underestimation. Agent Jones, already independently tracking the threat and converging on the same objective, translates Smith's command into coordinated, building-wide action with a nod and a touch to his earpiece — convergence dressed as compliance. The scene closes with all three Agents re-tasked from containment to total destruction.
events.action: The building's attack — fire alarms, explosions, and triggered sprinklers reaching the office — cracks Smith's composure into personal fury and drives all three Agents to recognize the intrusion as an active assault, converting it into a coordinated hunt under a kill order.

affects_outside.enables: The coordinated, building-wide hunt that the intruders must now evade — the rescue's success immediately triggers its counterattack.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Any remaining ambiguity about the Agents' intent: the pursuit is now unambiguously a kill order, closing off containment or capture as options.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: AGENT SMITH — the crack in his composure here becomes the personal vengeance that will drive him independently of the tactical objective in later events, long after the intruders are lost.

events.turns_on: The building's attack — fire alarms, explosions, and triggered sprinklers — is the pivot. It enters as an ambiguous disturbance the Agents are still interpreting analytically, changes into a confirmed open assault that cracks Smith's composure into fury and forces recognition of the escalation, and exits as the established fact that re-tasks the pursuit from containment to total destruction.

Whether Brown's 'They are actually attacking' is a genuine independent recognition or merely a status report awaiting Smith's command — the scene positions him as first to read the escalation but does not fully resolve his autonomy from Smith.

events.boundary_reason: The story cuts to the Agents' command response, a distinct beat where they shift from interrogation to actively hunting Neo and Trinity.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Fire alarms, explosions, and triggered sprinklers reach the executive office and confirm to the Agents that the intruders have moved from intrusion to open assault. Smith converts that shock into a kill order — 'Find them and destroy them' — while Brown names the escalation as fact and Jones immediately begins coordinating a building-wide search through his earpiece. The scene closes with the pursuit re-tasked from containment to total destruction.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The building's attack (alarms, explosions, sprinklers) forces the three Agents to recognize the intrusion as an active assault and to convert it into a coordinated hunt.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The building's attack — fire alarms, explosions, and triggered sprinklers — is the pivot: it is what forces the Agents' recognition and Smith's kill order. It enters as an ambiguous disturbance the Agents are still interpreting, changes into a confirmed open assault on the system, and exits as the established fact that re-tasks the pursuit from containment to destruction.

events.title: Rooftop battle with Agent Jones and the helicopter escape prep
events.summary: Agent Jones, embodied in the PILOT's body, closes on the wounded Neo atop the fallen enemies and cannot be stopped by gunfire; Neo, moving for the first time at Agent-speed, is winged in the shoulder and thigh and knocked down with Jones standing over him. Trinity arrives and fires a .45 round jammed tight to Jones's head, reverting him to the inert, motionless body of the PILOT, then helps Neo to his feet. Neo checks his shoulder, declares himself fine, and urges the pair toward the helicopter as the only exit. Unable to fly it herself, Trinity calls Tank aboard the hovercraft, who locates the military B-212 pilot program and loads it into her link; the download floods her with the essentials of flight, and she declares them ready to leave.
events.action: Trinity fires a .45 round into Agent Jones's head at point-blank range, reverting him to the inert body of the PILOT and ending the immediate lethal threat; she helps the wounded Neo up, Neo pushes the pair toward the helicopter, and Trinity has Tank load a B-212 pilot program into her link so she can fly them out.

He measures himself against a threshold he doesn't yet know he's meant to reach, so he experiences a staggering first success as a shortfall.

events.turns_on: Trinity's point-blank .45 kill shot into Agent Jones's head — the act that reverts the Agent to the inert PILOT's body, removes the immediate threat, and buys the seconds needed to load the helicopter-pilot program and prepare the escape.

events.boundary_reason: The action moves to the roof where Neo and Trinity fight Jones, and the immediate aftermath is their scramble to get the helicopter flying — a single continuous fight-and-escape unit that ends once Trinity has the piloting program loaded.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: On the rooftop, Agent Jones — having dissolved the PILOT into static and taken his body — closes on the wounded Neo and cannot be stopped by gunfire. Trinity arrives at the last instant and fires a round point-blank into Jones's head, reverting him to the inert body of the PILOT. Neo, shaken by having moved for the first time at Agent-speed but judging it 'not fast enough,' pushes the pair toward the helicopter. Trinity, unable to fly it, calls Tank aboard the hovercraft, who locates and loads a military B-212 pilot program into her link; the download floods her mind with the essentials of flight, and she declares them ready to leave.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Trinity shoots Agent Jones at point-blank range, reverting him to the host body; Neo and Trinity regroup and, with Tank loading a helicopter-pilot program into Trinity in real time, prepare to escape the rooftop by air.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Trinity's point-blank kill shot into Agent Jones's head — the act that reverts the Agent to the PILOT's body and ends the immediate threat, buying the seconds needed to prepare the helicopter escape.

events.title: The helicopter assault and Morpheus's rescue
events.summary: From a hovering helicopter, Neo guns down Agents Jones and Brown with the mounted .50 caliber gun; Agent Smith comprehends the seriousness of the assault, fires back, and is shot dead too — only to reconstitute upright in the shattered window and keep firing at the fleeing craft. Finding Morpheus slumped and unresponsive in his chair, Neo enters the office, rigs a climbing rope to his harness, and dives out the window to catch Morpheus mid-fall after Morpheus revives, snaps his handcuffs, runs for the window, and is shot in the leg. Neo is yanked off his feet by the rope as the dying helicopter drags it, but levers himself onto the rain gutter. Trinity, piloting the craft away under Smith's fire, loses the machine, crash-lands it toward the nearest roof, lunges out the back door, grabs the rope one-handed, and fires her gun to sever the cord — leaving the crew alive but exposed on the rooftop as the helicopter explodes against a skyscraper. The three Marines posted outside the office blister with snow-static as the Matrix destabilises.

events.title: Survivors regroup; Tank's realization and arranging the exit
events.summary: Across the Main Deck and a rooftop, the crew survives the rescue and re-forms. Tank, watching from the operator's chair in suspense, reaches certitude that Neo is the One, then is relieved and giddy when Morpheus's voice on the phone proves the crew lived; Morpheus asks him for the exit and relies on him to have it ready. On the rooftop, Morpheus converts the impossible rescue into confirmation of the prophecy: he reframes the Oracle's words as purposeful, delivers the 'knowing a path / walking a path' teaching, and presses Trinity, reading her silent look as affirmation. He cuts off Neo's attempt to report that the Oracle said he is not the One, so the contradiction is absorbed rather than heard. Neo embraces Trinity but is shut out by Morpheus, left holding the gap between the crew's public confirmation of him as the One and his private knowledge. Morpheus then calls Tank from the field for an exit, learns it is wired at the subway (State and Balbo), and heads there with Neo and Trinity. The event leaves the crew alive, reconnected, and moving toward the exit — but with Neo's contradiction suppressed rather than settled.

events.title: The Agents track the fugitives; Smith senses them
events.summary: On a rooftop, Brown completes a trace and reports the crew's position; Jones converts it into a command and orders a Sentinel strike. Smith breaks from the unit's procedural satisfaction, treating the escape as a personal insult and insisting the quarry is not yet gone, withdrawing to the rooftop edge and turning his back on Brown and Jones. The crew reaches a subway station and exits one by one through a ringing phone: Morpheus enters the booth, answers, and vanishes through the line, leaving the booth empty, with Neo and Trinity following toward the phone. An old man, previously unnoticed in a far corner, watches Morpheus disappear, reacts with recognition, and his eyes glow white.

events.title: The crew urges Neo to run as he resolves to fight
events.summary: From the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, Trinity urgently commands Neo to run, but Neo — alone in the subway, having apparently assessed the dead escalator as an escape route — turns his back on it and faces back toward his pursuer, his eyes taking on a fixed, hard gunfighter's quality. Watching on the deck, Trinity cannot interpret his refusal to flee and reads his stillness as confusion or a death wish, masking her fear as flat cognitive puzzlement; Morpheus, by contrast, sees visible confirmation of his prophetic framework in that same stillness and declares that Neo is beginning to believe, becoming the sole authoritative interpreter who reframes Trinity's fear for her.
events.action: Trinity commands Neo to run; Neo abandons the escape route and turns to face his pursuer with gunfighter's resolve; Trinity fails to parse his non-flight and masks fear as puzzlement; Morpheus reads the same stillness as the beginning of belief and declares it to Trinity.

events.title: Neo and Smith's subway duel
events.summary: Neo and Agent Smith fight to a parity in the subway, then that parity collapses: after a gunfight ends with both weapons empty, Smith shifts to hand-to-hand and gains the upper hand, driving Neo to near-death by the third-rail until Neo refuses the name and death Smith imposes, reverses the choke-hold and escapes onto the escalator — only for Smith to burst from the passing train in unharmed pursuit.
events.action: sc-182 opens with Neo and Smith firing simultaneously, the gunfight freezing into a mirrored standoff with guns jammed to each other's heads; when Smith taunts that Neo is empty, Neo answers 'So are you' and both triggers CLICK empty, shattering Smith's composure into rage as he switches to bare hands, cutting Neo and driving him back. sc-183 cuts to the hovercraft where Neo's real body convulses and coughs blood as his life signs spike, and Trinity realizes aloud that someone is killing him. sc-184 returns to the subway: Smith pins Neo against the tunnel wall by the electrified third-rail, drop-kicks him onto the tracks and locks a choke-hold as a train approaches; Neo, unable to breathe and 'not ready to die,' declares 'My name is Neo,' surges upward to smash Smith into the ceiling, backflips clear as the train barrels over Smith, and runs for the escalator — but the train's last-car doors open and Smith bursts out, glasses intact, in furious pursuit.

registers.change: Cut on the forearm, kicked against a steel column, then choked until his veins bulge and he cannot breathe — but at the moment of near-death he refuses and surges with impossible strength, smashing Smith into the ceiling and backflipping free.
registers.exit: Exhausted but unbroken, having escaped the choke-hold and reached the escalator, knees shaking as he runs.

registers.entry: An equal matched against the Agent — proven by the mutual empty-click.
registers.change: Driven back and overpowered by Smith's hand-to-hand fury, nearly killed, then reverses the power dynamic by refusing the name and fate Smith imposes.
registers.exit: No longer prey being hunted down — but not victorious either; he is a fugitive running from a pursuer who cannot be shaken.

registers.change: Learns through being nearly killed that force alone will not win this fight; his surge comes only when he stops accepting the rules and the name ('Mr. Anderson') Smith assigns him.
registers.exit: Knows he can escape this kill, but does not yet know Smith cannot be killed — he believes distance and the train end the threat, which the next scene disproves.

registers.exit: Fierce with self-assertion but still afraid, running on adrenaline and shaking knees.

registers.exit: On the escalator, running up and away from the tracks toward the exit.

events.title: The Siren Sounds — Sentinels Arrive
events.summary: Aboard the hovercraft, the crew's tracking of Neo on the Matrix feed is severed when a siren declares the ship itself the target of an incoming Sentinel attack. Tank, losing Neo's signal at the moment the feed cuts, reads the worst case — caught or dead — before Morpheus's order re-forms his alarm into procedure as he charges the E.M.P. Morpheus bolts to the cockpit, reads the Sentinels on the radar, sets the five-to-six-minute window, and orders the weapon armed. Trinity, having just watched Neo's body convulse, learns the deadline and opposes the order: the one defense cannot be fired without killing Neo if he is still jacked in, and she reads Morpheus's readiness to arm it as willingness to sacrifice Neo. Morpheus overrides her objection not with argument but with the reassurance that Neo will make it — faith grounded in the prophecy, stated as fact to steady her, though he has no confirmation.
events.action: The crew transitions from tracking Neo's combat in the Matrix to defending the ship against an incoming Sentinel attack: the siren reclassifies the ship as the target, Morpheus assumes command and orders the E.M.P. charged on a fixed five-to-six-minute countdown, and Trinity moves from asking for information to open opposition over the weapon's lethal effect on Neo if fired while he is still jacked in.

Trinity, having just watched Neo nearly killed, objects that the weapon cannot be made ready while Neo is still jacked in; Morpheus overrides her fear with the assurance that Neo will make it back. events.title: Neo's Foot Chase for an Exit
events.summary: Fleeing on foot through the city with no way to reach the ship, Neo steals a Businessman's cell phone and dials the crew to demand extraction, believing contact means he is essentially safe — only to learn the robbed man is Agent Smith. Smith sheds his civilian disguise, closes the distance down an alley, and opens fire at close range, turning the pursuit lethal while Neo remains un-routed. Over the comms, Tank searches blind for a viable exit under the closing threat, and Trinity escalates to screaming commands, pressing Neo to move faster as the crew races a deadline to get him out.
events.action: Neo steals a Businessman's cell phone mid-sprint, dials long distance to the ship, and runs into an alley with Smith gaining; he reaches the crew and demands extraction as Tank answers and Trinity joins the line. The robbed Businessman is revealed to be Agent Smith, who closes the gap, stops, aims, and fires at Neo at close range. Tank searches for a viable exit under active pressure while Trinity screams urgent commands that Neo answers, and Neo keeps running under direct fire, still not routed to an exit.

events.title: Up Through the Building to the Fire Escape
events.summary: Steered entirely by Tank's voice from the ship, Neo flees up the interior staircase of the old crooked apartment building, is redirected through the hall and two apartments, throws open a window (a knife burying itself in its casing as doors explode and are perforated behind him), leaps onto the fire escape, and drops ten feet into the alley, where he lands broken and bleeding and sprints for its far end. Tank, watching Neo's position on the ship's monitor, corrects his wrong-door mistake ('Other left!'), directs him to the window and fire escape, tells him to go 'Down! Down!', and announces that Neo has nearly reached the fire escape while steering him toward the alley's end. Agent Brown closes the distance through the building and appears on the fire escape directly behind Neo as Neo drops into the alley. The event moves Neo from interior flight to the open alley, one step ahead but physically degraded, with the pursuer now directly behind him.

events.boundary_reason: Neo climbs the stairs, is steered by Tank's voice through the hall and out a window to the fire escape, lands broken below, and Tank confirms he's nearly at the fire escape. The unit tracks his vertical ascent and Tank's guidance. sc-201 cuts to Smith pausing in recognition of the hotel — a beat outside Neo's flight that reframes the pursuit.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Steered entirely by Tank's voice from the ship, Neo flees upward and across the apartment building — springing up the staircase, being redirected through apartments under gunfire, and leaping onto the fire escape into the alley — while Agent Brown closes in behind him. The event moves Neo from interior flight to the open alley, still one step ahead of his pursuer, and keeps the pursuer's identity off-screen.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Neo is guided by Tank through the building and out to the alley fire escape, with Agent Brown in pursuit.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: fire escape — the escape route Neo must reach to leave the building; Tank's guidance converges on it and Neo's leap onto it is the event's pivot.

events.title: Smith Recognizes the Hotel as the Sentinels Strike
events.summary: Agent Smith halts outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, arrested by recognition of the place. Simultaneously, in the Nebuchadnezzar, Tank moves to dial Neo out himself, but the Sentinels arrive and breach the ship's concealment; the hull is struck, the extraction is aborted, and Morpheus arms the EMP detonator as the crew registers that their pursuers are on them.
events.action: Recognition on the street coincides with the Sentinels locating and striking the hidden hovercraft, converting the extraction's forward momentum into open jeopardy and forcing the crew onto the EMP as the ship's last defense.

events.boundary_reason: Smith halts at the Heart O' The City Hotel, then the story cuts to the crew readying Neo's exit as the sentinels physically attack the ship — lights go red, the Nebuchadnezzar is struck, and Morpheus readies the EMP. This final run converges the two threats (Smith closing in, sentinels attacking) at the extraction point. It is the last material given.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Agent Smith halts outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, arrested by recognition of the place. events.title: Trinity's vigil and Neo's revival
events.summary: Amid the ship's destruction on the main deck, Trinity takes hold of Neo's body, recounts the Oracle's prophecy that she would fall in love with 'the one,' declares her love for him twice, and kisses him; Morpheus weeps over Neo and takes hold of the EMP switch, poised to trigger it; in the Matrix, Agent Brown checks Neo's vital signs and reports 'He's gone,' and Agent Smith dismisses him; then the ship's monitors jump back to life and Trinity screams and shouts for Neo to get up, while in the Matrix his eyes snap open.
events.action: Trinity takes hold of Neo's body, recounts the Oracle's prophecy, declares her love for him twice, and kisses him; Morpheus weeps and takes hold of the EMP switch; Agent Brown checks Neo's vital signs and reports 'He's gone,' and Agent Smith bids the dead man farewell; the ship's monitors jump back to life, Tank shares a look with Morpheus, and Trinity screams and commands Neo to rise, while in the Matrix his eyes snap open.

events.title: Neo sees the code and destroys Agent Smith
events.summary: In the hall, the wounded Neo halts the Agents' bullets in midair, plucks one, lets the rest fall, and now sees the walls, floor, and Agents dissolve into a rushing stream of code. He enters Agent Smith's body and bursts out of him, destroying Smith in a brilliant explosion of light that the Matrix absorbs. The remaining Agents, seized by fear for the first time, look at each other and flee the hall. On the ship's deck, Tank, Morpheus, and Trinity watch the scrolling code resolve into live images of Neo; Tank can only ask 'How...?!' while Morpheus declares him the One and Trinity holds her relief in silence — all of it cut short when an explosion rocks the ship.
events.action: Neo's immunity in the hall inverts the enforcer hierarchy: he stops the bullets, sees the world as code, destroys Agent Smith, and routs the remaining Agents, while his crew witnesses his return and Morpheus affirms him as the One — an affirmation undercut when an explosion strikes the ship.

events.title: The ship is overrun and the EMP is triggered
events.summary: Sentinels overrun the ship and begin destroying it while the crew converges on the ringing phone as their only exit; Trinity directs the escape with her call for Neo and her 'Now!' cue, Morpheus acts on that cue to turn the key and trigger the EMP, and the white light kills the machines, dropping their cold carcasses into the overflow pit as Neo dives for the phone.
events.action: The ship is overrun by sentinels that begin destroying it, forcing the crew to use the ringing phone as their last way out. Trinity directs the escape — calling for Neo, then giving the 'Now!' cue for the key. Morpheus acts on that cue without hesitation and turns the key, triggering the EMP. A blinding shock of white light floods the chamber and instantly kills the sentinels, leaving their cold metal carcasses filling the overflow pit. Neo dives for the phone as the ship dies around him.

events.turns_on: The event turns on Trinity's two-part command — her call for Neo and her 'Now!' cue — which are the two ends of one decision to get the crew off before the ship dies; on the ringing phone as the single exit the overrun forces everyone toward; and on the EMP, the white light that flips the sentinels from an overrunning swarm into dead carcasses in a single instant.

prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The event turns on the EMP — the white light that flips the sentinels from an overrunning swarm into dead carcasses — and on the ringing phone, the single exit the whole overrun forces the crew toward.

events.title: Neo wakes and addresses the Matrix
events.summary: In the still darkness of the hovercraft, Trinity's voice calls Neo back from death; his eyes open, he reaches for her, and she weeps with relief before they kiss. Neo's voice then addresses an unseen audience in the Matrix, declaring he is done running and hiding and that they will not have to search for him anymore. He frames the conflict as a choice he is offering the machines: the Matrix can remain a cage or become a chrysalis, and to be free one must change oneself rather than one's cage. He speaks with resolve rather than fear, leaving only whether he is done fighting up to them.
events.action: Trinity speaks and Neo revives, reaching for her; she weeps and they kiss. The scene then moves into Neo's voice addressing someone in the Matrix: he renounces flight and concealment, ends his own pursuit, and offers the choice between the Matrix as cage or chrysalis, teaching that freedom comes from changing oneself rather than the cage.

registers.exit: No longer prey — resolved and self-possessed, standing openly and addressing the machines directly, leaving only whether he is 'done fighting' up to them.

state_triples.reading: Neo believes he is no longer being offered a choice he must fear — he has already chosen. He treats the machines not as hunters to evade but as an audience to be persuaded, convinced that the real battlefield is the mind's willingness to change itself rather than the cage's walls.

state_triples.reading: Trinity reads the revival as the impossible reversed — the grief she had already surrendered to is suddenly void, and the tears she cannot stop are the discharge of a vigil she believed had ended in loss. She lets her guard fall completely here because the dark, emptied hovercraft is the one place with no one left to perform for.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's public declaration that he is 'done running, done hiding' and his reframing of the Matrix as a potential chrysalis set the terms for the coming phase of the war — he now addresses the machines/those in the Matrix directly rather than evading them.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's concealment as a strategy is spent; he can no longer be treated as a hidden fugitive, which removes the option of hiding for the resistance's key figure.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Whoever answered the ringing phone on the Matrix side now holds Neo's open challenge and his cage-or-chrysalis offer, positioning them to respond to a target that has voluntarily revealed itself.

events.turns_on: The pivot from private revival to public address — Neo moving from the intimate kiss with Trinity into a deliberate voice that speaks to an audience in the Matrix, converting his exposure from hunted prey into a chosen stance and reframing the conflict from a chase into a choice offered to the machines.

carried_uncertainty.what: Who exactly answers the ringing phone on the Matrix side and whether Neo's audience is the machines, other plugged-in humans, or both.
Whether the hovercraft is moving, powered down, or in any particular state beyond 'still darkness.'

events.boundary_reason: This scene pivots from the battle's resolution to the film's closing statement; it is self-contained (reunion + the phone-call monologue), and sc-224 is the physical departure that follows, so it stands alone as the pivot.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: In the still darkness of the hovercraft, Trinity's voice calls Neo back; his eyes open, he reaches for her, and she weeps with relief before they kiss. The scene then reframes around a computer screen and a ringing phone: Neo's voice addresses an unseen audience in the Matrix, declaring he is done running and hiding, offering them the choice between keeping the Matrix a cage or letting it become a chrysalis, and telling them freedom comes from changing oneself rather than one's cage.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Trinity speaks Neo's name and he revives, reaching for her; she weeps and they kiss. The scene dissolves to a computer screen whose cursor beats steadily, a phone rings and is answered, and a trace program fills the screen as Neo's voice-over addresses someone in the Matrix.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The ringing phone and its answer — the event pivots on the phone being picked up on the Matrix side, which is what converts Neo's private revival into a public address to an audience; without that connection his declaration has no recipient.

events.title: Neo hangs up and takes flight
events.summary: Neo ends a phone call, steps out of a street-level booth, and launches into flight, rising until the city is miles below and moving faster than a speeding bullet. He equips sunglasses and lets his coat stream behind him like a black leather cape, presenting himself not as a man escaping but as the myth others have projected onto him. The scene — and, by its fade-out, the story — closes on him as a superhuman figure moving with power and ease through the air.
events.action: Neo terminates the call, exits the street-level phone booth, equips sunglasses, and takes flight above the city with his coat streaming like a cape.

state_triples.reading: Neo reads his own ascent as a declaration rather than an escape — the sunglasses and the cape-like coat are chosen self-presentation, signalling that he now occupies the myth others have projected onto him rather than merely surviving it.

affects_outside.enables: Sets the terms for the story's closing beat — a figure who can fly unaided through the sky, having publicly shed the grounded man he was, is positioned to make a declaration to the world beyond.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Nothing is spent or closed off here; the beat opens possibility rather than consuming it.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: None recorded — no character outside the scene is shown reacting to or affected by this flight within the material given.

events.turns_on: Neo's transformation into a flyer — the event pivots on him crossing from a grounded, unadorned man into 'the One,' airborne and in full command of flight, with the sunglasses and cape-like coat marking that shift as chosen self-presentation rather than mere survival.

events.boundary_reason: The final image — Neo stepping out of the booth and flying over the city — is the closing beat, a distinct unit that ends the film.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Neo ends a phone call, leaves the booth, and launches into flight, rising above the city at superhuman speed. The scene — and, by its fade-out, the story — closes on him as a being in full command of the air rather than a man on the ground.

prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Neo's transformation into a flyer — the event pivots on him crossing from grounded man to airborne superhuman, which is itself the state change rather than a separate object.
